(p-252) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Hijr

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims.﴾

In this noble verse He mentions that when the disbelievers come to know the reality of the matter, they will wish that they had been Muslims in the worldly abode, and they will regret their disbelief. This meaning is expressed in other places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿If only you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire and say, "Oh, would that we were returned, and would not deny the signs of our Lord, and would be among the believers!"﴾ [al-An'am: 27]

• And His saying: ﴿Until, when the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they say, "Oh, our regret over what we neglected concerning it!"﴾ [al-An'am: 31]

• And His saying: ﴿And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands, saying, "Oh, would that I had taken with the Messenger a way!"﴾ [al-Furqan: 27]

and other verses. The statements of the scholars regarding this verse all return to one thing, because whoever says that the disbeliever, when he is at the point of death and witnesses the reality, wishes he had been a Muslim, and whoever says that when he sees the Fire and stands over it he wishes he had been a Muslim, and whoever says that when they witness the bringing out of the monotheists from the Fire they wish they had been Muslims, all of that returns to the fact that the disbelievers, when they witness the reality, regret disbelief and wish that they had been Muslims.

Nafi' and 'Asim read "rubama" with the ba' lightened (rubama, with light tashdid-less ba'), while the rest read it with the ba' emphasized (shaddah). The lightened form is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz, and the emphasized form is the dialect of Tamim, Qays and Rabi'ah. From the first is the saying of 'Adi ibn al-Ra'la' al-Ghassani:

"Rubama darbatin bi-saifin saqilin bayna Busra wa-ta'natin najla'"

The second is very common, and from it is the saying of another:

"Ala rubama ahdat laki al-'ayn nazratan / qisaraki minha annaha 'anki la tujdi"

Regarding "rubba" in this place, some scholars said it is for multiplication, meaning: the disbelievers will wish, at many times, that they had been Muslims. Al-Qurtubi transmitted this view from the Kufans, saying: from it is the saying of the poet:

"Ala rubama ahdat laki al-'ayn ..."

the verse.

Some scholars said: here it is for diminution, because they said that in some situations and not in all of them, due to their being occupied with the punishment. If it is said: "Rubama" does not enter except upon the past tense, so what is the reason for its entry upon the present tense in this place? The answer: when Allah, exalted is He, promised the occurrence of that, that promise became a certainty of its occurrence, like what has already occurred, and its parallel is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The command of Allah has come﴾ (the verse) [al-Nahl: 1] and similar verses, so He expressed with the past tense, treating the certainty of occurrence as the position of an actual occurrence.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 3:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, and let hope distract them; but they will come to know.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah threatens the disbelievers by commanding His Prophet ﷺ to leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, for they will come to know the reality of what the matter will lead to, namely the severity of their punishment and humiliation. He threatens them with this kind of threat in other passages, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Say: "Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire."﴾ [Ibrahim: 30] (The verse number given in the source is [14], which is a reference to the surah's own numbering.)

• His saying: ﴿Eat and enjoy yourselves a little; indeed you are criminals.﴾ [al-Mursalat: 46]

• His saying: ﴿Say: "Enjoy your disbelief a little; indeed you are among the companions of the Fire."﴾ [al-Zumar: 8]

• His saying: ﴿So leave them to wade in falsehood and play, until they meet their Day which they are promised.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 83], [al-Ma'arij: 42]

• His saying: ﴿So leave them until they meet their Day in which they will be struck senseless.﴾ [al-Tur: 45]

And other verses besides these.

It has been established in the science of rhetoric (fann al-ma'ani) and in the discussion of the imperative (al-amr) among the usuliyyun (jurists of legal theory) that among the meanings for which the form of the imperative (if'al) is used is threat, as in the verse mentioned, and His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: "dharhum," meaning "utruk-hum" (leave them). This verb is only used in the imperative and the present tense. Its past tense is taraka, its verbal noun is al-tark, its active participle is tarik, and its passive participle is matruk. Some scholars said: this verse is abrogated by the verses of the sword, and Allah knows best. Al-Qurtubi said: "al-Amal (hope) is greed for this world, clinging to it, loving it, and turning away from the Hereafter." And it is related from al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: "No servant has prolonged hope except that he has done evil deeds." We have already presented the remedy for prolonged hope in Surat al-Baqarah.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they said, "O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, indeed you are mad."﴾ It may be asked concerning this noble verse: how do they acknowledge that the Reminder was sent down to him, and yet attribute madness to him at the same time? The answer is that their saying ﴿O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down﴾ means, according to their claim, a mockery on their part directed at him. What clarifies this meaning is the occurrence of similar speech from the disbelievers who mocked the messengers, peace and blessings of Allah be upon them, in other places, such as the words of Allah, the Exalted, concerning Pharaoh with Moses: He said, ﴿Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is mad﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 27] (p-254), and His words concerning the people of Shu'ayb, ﴿Indeed, you are surely the forbearing, the discerning﴾. [11:87]

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 7:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Why do you not bring us the angels, if you are among the truthful?﴾ Here, "law ma" (لَوْ ما) in this noble verse is for tahdiid (تَحْضِيض, urging), which is the demand for an action in an urgent manner. The meaning of the verse is that the disbelievers demanded of the Prophet ﷺ a specific demand, that he bring them the angels, so that the coming of the angels with him would be a proof of his truthfulness that he is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He clarified this demand of the disbelievers in other verses,

such as His saying about Pharaoh, along with Musa: ﴿Why have bracelets of gold not been bestowed upon him, or the angels not come with him in succession?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 53]

and His saying: ﴿And those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Why were the angels not sent down to us, or [why] do we not see our Lord?" Certainly they have been arrogant within themselves and have transgressed with great insolence.﴾ [al-Furqan: 21]

and His saying: ﴿And they say, "Why has an angel not been sent down to him?" And if We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-An'am: 8]

and His saying: ﴿Why has an angel not been sent down to him so that he would be a warner along with him?﴾ [al-Furqan: 7]

and His saying: ﴿Or you bring about Allah and the angels as a guarantee.﴾ [al-Isra': 92]

and other verses besides these.

Know that "law" (لَوْ) is combined with "la" (لا) and "ma" (ما) for two meanings. The first of them is tahdiid (التَّحْضِيض, urging), and its example is "law ma" in this noble verse, and its example with "lawla" is the saying of Jarir:

*You count the slaughter of the she-camels the best of your glory, O sons of Dhawtara, rather than the armoured warrior who is veiled.*

That is, "Why do you not count the veiled armoured warrior?" The second meaning is the prevention of something due to the existence of something else, and this occurs very frequently with "lawla," such as the saying of Amir ibn al-Akwa' - may Allah be pleased with him:

*By Allah, had it not been for Allah, we would not have been guided, nor would we have given charity, nor would we have prayed.*

And its example with "law ma" is the saying of Ibn Muqbil:

*Were it not for shame, and were it not for religion, I would have reproached you both for some of what is in you, when you reproached me for my defect.*

As for "hal" (هَلْ), it is combined only with "la" alone for tahdiid.

Note

The particles of tahdiid may come for reproach and rebuke, in which case they are restricted to the past or what is in its meaning, such as His saying: ﴿Why was there not a city that believed so that its faith would have benefited it, except the people of Yunus?﴾ up to the end of the verse [Yunus: 98], and His saying: ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it?﴾ up to the end of the verse [an-Nur: 13], and His saying: ﴿Why did those they had taken as gods other than Allah, as an offering, not help them?﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-Ahqaf: 28]. Some of them considered Jarir's saying, "You count the slaughter of the she-camels," the verse mentioned just above, to be of this type, saying that his intention is to rebuke them for not counting the veiled armoured warrior in the past.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 8:

The statement of Allah the Exalted: ﴿We send not down the angels except with truth, and they would not then be given respite.﴾

In this noble verse, He, may His majesty be exalted, makes clear that He sends down the angels only with truth, meaning with revelation. It was also said: with punishment. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Except as a descent accompanied by wisdom and benefit. There is no wisdom in the angels coming to you visibly, such that you see them and they bear witness to you of the truthfulness of the Prophet (ﷺ), for then you would believe out of compulsion." He said: "A similar statement is His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿We created not the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾ [al-Hijr: 85]."

In this noble verse He, the Exalted, also makes clear that if the angels were sent down upon them, they would not be given respite. This is in His statement: ﴿and they would not then be given respite﴾ [al-Hijr: 8], because the tanwin in His statement (idhan) is a substitute for a clause, so it contains a condition and a response. The sense is: "Even if the angels were sent down upon them, they would not be given respite," meaning not granted delay by postponing the punishment from them. This meaning is made clear in other places, such as His statement: ﴿On the Day they see the angels, there will be no good news that Day for the guilty﴾ [al-Furqan: 22], and His statement: ﴿And if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and then they would not be reprieved﴾ [al-An'am: 8], and other verses.

As for His statement ﴿We send not down the angels﴾ [al-Hijr: 8], Hafs, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read (nunazzilu) with two nuns, the first dammed and the second fathah, with the shadda on the zay kasrah, and (al-mala'ikata) in the accusative as the direct object of (nunazzilu). Shu'bah read (tunazzalu) with a damma on the taa' and a fathah on the nun, with the zay shaddah fathah, in the passive voice, and (al-mala'ikatu) in the nominative as the deputy subject of (tunazzalu). The rest read (tanazzalu) with a fathah on the taa', the nun and the zay shaddah. Its original form is (tatanazzalu), and one of the two taa's was elided, and (al-mala'ikatu) is in the nominative as the subject of (tanazzalu), like His statement: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein﴾ [al-Qadr: 4].

The Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian.﴾

In this noble verse, He (exalted is He) makes clear that it is He who sent down the Great Qur'an, and that He is its guardian against anything being added to it, or taken from it, or any part of it being altered or changed. He clarified this same meaning in other places, such as His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is a Mighty Book. Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or behind it; it is a revelation from the All-Wise, Praiseworthy﴾ [Fussilat: 41-42], and His saying: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 16] up to His saying: ﴿Then indeed, upon Us is its explanation﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 19]. This is the correct interpretation of the meaning of this verse: that the pronoun in His saying ﴿and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr: 9] (p-256) refers to the Reminder, which is the Qur'an. It has been said that the pronoun refers to the Prophet (ﷺ), as in His saying: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67]. But the first view is the correct one, as is apparent from the obvious context.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 15, verse 16:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We have certainly placed in the sky constellations (buruj)﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, may He be exalted, makes clear that He placed constellations in the sky. He mentioned this also in other places, such as His saying: ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations﴾ [Al-Furqan: 61], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And by the sky containing the constellations﴾ [Al-Buruj: 1]. The word buruj is the plural of burj (lit. "tower"; here, a constellation or stellar mansion).

The scholars differed about the meaning of al-buruj in the mentioned verses. Some said: al-buruj are the stars (kawakib). Among those reported to have said this are Mujahid and Qatadah. It is reported from Abu Salih that they are the great stars. It was also said that they are palaces in the sky, guarded by sentinels; Atiyyah was among those who held this view. It was said that they are the stations (manazil) of the sun and the moon, as stated by Ibn Abbas. The names of these constellations are: Aries (al-Hamal), Taurus (al-Thawr), Gemini (al-Jawza'), Cancer (al-Saratan), Leo (al-Asad), Virgo (al-Sunbulah), Libra (al-Mizan), Scorpio (al-Aqrab), Sagittarius (al-Qaws), Capricorn (al-Jady), Aquarius (al-Dalw), and Pisces (al-Hut).

The one who restricts this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: In Surah an-Nisa', Allah, may He be exalted, used buruj to refer to fortified palaces, in His saying: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be in towers built up high﴾ [An-Nisa': 78]. All of these sayings return to one thing, because the original meaning of buruj in the language is manifestness (al-zuhur). From it comes tabarruj (a woman's display), by showing her adornment. Thus the stars are manifest, the palaces are manifest, and the stations of the moon and the sun are like palaces, by the common factor that each is a place in which one alights. And knowledge is with Allah, may He be exalted.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We have adorned it for the observers﴾. In this noble verse, Allah, may He be exalted, states explicitly that He adorned the sky for the observers. In other places He clarified that He adorned it with the stars, and that this is the lowest heaven, as in His saying: ﴿And We have certainly adorned the lowest heaven with lamps﴾ [Al-Mulk: 5], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have adorned the lowest heaven with the adornment of the stars﴾ [As-Saffat: 6].

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 17 (part 1 of 3):**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We guarded it from every accursed devil﴾ ﴿except one who eavesdrops, and he is pursued by a clear flame﴾. In this noble verse, He, exalted is He, has stated explicitly that He guarded the sky from every accursed devil, and He clarified this meaning in other places,

• such as His saying: ﴿And a guard against every rebellious devil﴾ [As-Saffat: 7]

• and His saying: ﴿And We have made them missiles against the devils﴾ [Al-Mulk: 5]

• and His saying: ﴿Whoever now listens will find for himself a watching flame﴾ [Al-Jinn: 9]

• and His saying: ﴿Indeed, they are removed from hearing﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 212]

• and His saying: ﴿Or do they have a ladder by which they eavesdrop? Then let their eavesdropper bring a clear authority﴾ [At-Tur: 38]

and other verses besides these.

As for the exception (al-istithna', exception) in this noble verse, in His saying: ﴿except one who eavesdrops, and he is pursued by a clear flame﴾ [Al-Hijr: 18]. Some scholars said: it is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati', an exception whose excluded item does not belong to the category of what precedes it), and al-Fakhr al-Razi affirmed it. The meaning is: "But whoever eavesdrops, that is, snatches a brief snatch, a flame pursues him and burns him," like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they are pelted from every side﴾ ﴿repelled, and for them is a constant punishment﴾ ﴿except one who snatches a snatch, so a piercing flame pursues him﴾ [As-Saffat: 8-10]. It was also said: the exception is a connected exception (istithna' muttasil, an exception whose excluded item belongs to the category of what precedes it). The meaning is: We guarded the sky from the devils, so that they would not hear anything of the revelation or other things, except one who eavesdrops. For We did not guard it from listening to news of the heavens other than the revelation. As for the revelation, they hear nothing of it, because of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, they are removed from hearing﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 212]. This was said by al-Qurtubi. Its parallel is ﴿except one who snatches﴾, the verse [As-Saffat: 10], for it is an exception from the waw (the plural subject) in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly﴾, the verse [As-Saffat: 8].

* *

[The Owners of Artificial Satellites]

* *

Warning

It is understood from these verses that we mentioned that everything that the owners of artificial satellites boast of, that they will reach the sky and build upon the moon, is all lies and empty chatter with no substance beneath it. It is of the certainty that has no doubt that they will stop at their limit and return humiliated, abased, and incapable: ﴿Then return the gaze twice; the gaze will return to you humbled and weary﴾ [Al-Mulk: 4]. The way the aforementioned verses indicate this is that the Arabic tongue, in which the Qur'an was revealed, applies the name "devil" to every defiant rebel among the jinn, humans, and beasts. From it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they go privately to their devils, they say, "Indeed, we are with you"﴾, the verse [Al-Baqarah: 14], and His saying: ﴿And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy, devils of mankind and jinn, inspiring to one another decorative speech as deception﴾ [Al-An'am: 112]. From it is also His saying (ﷺ): "The black dog is a devil," and the verse of Jarir:

*Days when they called me "the devil" because of my ghazal (love poetry), and they used to desire me when I was a devil.*

There is no doubt that the owners of artificial satellites enter the category of devils in the first instance, because of their insolence and defiance. Once you know this, know that He, exalted is He, stated explicitly that the sky is guarded from every devil, whoever he may be, in a number of verses of His Book, such as His saying here: ﴿And We guarded it from every accursed devil﴾ [Al-Hijr: 17], and His saying: ﴿And a guard. That is the decree of the Mighty, the Knowing﴾ [Fussilat: 12], and other verses besides these.

He also stated explicitly that whoever intends to eavesdrop is pursued by a flame that lies in wait for him, in other places,

• such as His saying: ﴿Whoever now listens will find for himself a watching flame﴾ [Al-Jinn: 9]

• and His saying: ﴿except one who eavesdrops, and he is pursued by a clear flame﴾ [Al-Hijr: 18]

• and His saying: ﴿except one who snatches a snatch, so a piercing flame pursues him﴾ [As-Saffat: 9]. He said: ﴿Indeed, they are removed from hearing﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 212]. He said: ﴿Or do they have a ladder by which they eavesdrop? Then let their eavesdropper bring a clear authority﴾ [At-Tur: 38]. This is a challenge (ta'jiz, a demonstration of incapacity), indicating the complete incapacity of humans for that. He said: ﴿Or do they have the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them? Then let them ascend by the means﴾ ﴿a host there, defeated from among the factions﴾ [Sad: 10-11]. So His saying in this noble verse: ﴿Then let them ascend by the means﴾, that is, let them climb by the means of the heavens by which they reach them. The imperative form in His saying: ﴿Then let them ascend﴾ is for challenge, and its use for challenge is evidence of human incapacity for that, complete incapacity. And His saying, glorified and exalted is He, after that challenge: ﴿a host there, defeated from among the factions﴾ [Sad: 11] implies that if a host from among the factions were to strive to ascend by the means of the sky, it would return defeated, humiliated, degraded. Among what indicates that this noble verse refers to something that the people at the time of its revelation did not suppose is that He, glorified and exalted is He, left that host indefinite with the word "ma" in His saying: "a host *ma* [there]" [Sad: 11], and His indication of the place of that host, or the place of its defeat, is the indication of the distant with His saying: "there" [Sad: 11]. Nothing preceding in the verse showed the reference of the indication to it, except the ascent by the means of the heavens.

So the noble verse is understood to mean what we mentioned. It is known that none of the scholars explained it that way. Rather, the expressions of the exegetes revolve around the fact that the host mentioned is the disbelievers who denied him (ﷺ), that he (ﷺ) would defeat them, and that this was realized on the day of Badr or the day of the Conquest of Makkah. But the wonders and marvels of the Book of Allah continue to appear renewed over the passing of nights and days, so at every moment things are understood from it that were not understood before. The narration of Abu Juhayfah, which is established in the Sahih, supports this: when he asked Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) whether the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had singled them out with anything, Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said to him: "No, by He who split the grain and created the soul, except an understanding that Allah gives a man concerning the Book of Allah, and what is in this sheet..." the hadith. So his saying (may Allah be pleased with him): "except an understanding that Allah gives a man concerning the Book of Allah" indicates that understanding of the Book of Allah renews knowledge and insights that were not available to ordinary people. There is no barrier to carrying the verse on what the exegetes carried it on.

What we mentioned also is understood from it, according to what has been established among the scholars, that if a verse can bear several meanings all of which are correct, it is necessary to carry it on all of them, as Shaykh Taqi al-Din Abu al-Abbas Ibn Taymiyya verified with his proofs in his treatise on the sciences of the Qur'an.

He, exalted is He, also stated explicitly that the moon is in the seven layers in His saying: ﴿Have you not considered how Allah created seven heavens in layers?﴾ ﴿and made the moon therein a light﴾ [Nuh: 15-16]. So it is known from the verses that the moon is in the seven layers, and that Allah guarded them from every accursed devil. Thus there remains no doubt or ambiguity that the devils, the owners of artificial satellites, will return humbled and degraded, incapable of reaching the moon and reaching the sky. There remains no ambiguity that the sky in which the moon is does not mean absolutely whatever is above you, although the word "sky" may be used linguistically for everything above you, like the roof of a house. From it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then let him stretch a rope to the sky﴾, the verse [Al-Hajj: 15]. The poet said:

*Everything elevated may be called "sky," but the excellence lies where the sun and the moon are.*

This is because of His explicit statement, exalted is He, that the moon is in the seven layers. The pronoun in His saying: ﴿and made the moon therein﴾ [Nuh: 16] refers to the seven layers, and the use of the whole where only a part is meant is common in the Qur'an and in the speech of the Arabs.

Among the clearest of its proofs is the reading of Hamzah and al-Kisa'i: ﴿And if they fight you, then kill them﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 191], from killing (qatl), in both verbs. For whoever is killed, in the passive voice, cannot be commanded after his death to kill his killer. Rather, the intended meaning is: if they kill some of you, then some others of you should kill them, as is evident.

Abu Hayyan said in al-Bahr al-Muhit, in his exegesis of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and made the moon therein a light﴾ [Nuh: 16]: It is valid for the heavens to be a container (zarf) for the moon, because it does not necessarily follow from the container that the contained fills it. You say: Zayd is in the city, and he is in a part of it.

Know that the wording of the verse is explicit that the moon itself is in the seven layers. This is because the word *ja'ala* ("made") in the verse [Nuh: 15] is the one meaning *sayyara* ("made into" or "turned into"), and it governs the subject and the predicate. What is expressed by the subject is exactly what is expressed by the predicate, not something else. So your saying: "I made the clay pottery, and the iron a ring," there is no hiding that the clay is exactly the pottery, and the iron is the ring. Likewise His saying: ﴿and made the moon therein a light﴾ [Nuh: 16].

So the light made therein is exactly the moon itself. Therefore it is not understood from the verse, according to the linguistic convention, that there is a possibility that the moon itself is outside the seven layers, and that what is placed in them is merely its light. For if that were meant, it would have said: "and made the light of the moon therein." As for His saying: ﴿and made the moon therein a light﴾, it is explicit that the light placed in them is the very moon. It is not permissible to turn the Qur'an away from its apparent meaning without a proof to which one must return. This is clarified by the fact that He, exalted is He, stated explicitly in Surat al-Furqan that the moon is in the sky specifically of the constellations, with His saying: ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations and placed therein a lamp and a luminous moon﴾ [Al-Furqan: 61]. And He stated explicitly in Surat al-Hijr that the constellations, in which the moon is stated to be, are exactly those guarded from every accursed devil, with His saying: ﴿And We have placed in the sky constellations and adorned them for the observers﴾ ﴿and guarded them from every accursed devil﴾ [Al-Hijr: 16-17].

As for what some people claim, that He, glorified and exalted is He, indicated the connection between the people of the sky and the people of the earth in His saying: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and what He has dispersed in them of creatures; and He is, over their gathering, when He wills, competent﴾ [Ash-Shura: 29], it is said concerning it that the intended meaning is their gathering on the Day of Resurrection in the place of assembly, as the exegetes agreed upon. What supports this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth, nor bird that flies with its two wings, but they are communities like you. We have not neglected in the Book anything. Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾ [Al-An'am: 38].

This is clarified by the naming of the Day of Resurrection as the Day of Gathering, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering, that is the day of mutual loss﴾, the verse [At-Taghabun: 9]. And there are many verses indicating that the gathering of all creatures takes place on the Day of Resurrection,

• such as His saying: ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a witnessed Day﴾ [Hud: 103]

• and His saying: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the first and the last will surely be gathered to the appointed time of a known Day"﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 49-50]

• and His saying: ﴿Allah, there is no deity but Him. He will surely gather you to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt﴾ [An-Nisa': 87]

• and His saying: ﴿And the Day the sky will be split open with clouds, and the angels will be sent down, descending﴾ [Al-Furqan: 25]

• and His saying: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angel, rank upon rank﴾ [Al-Fajr: 22]

• and His saying: ﴿And We gathered them, and We left none of them behind﴾ [Al-Kahf: 47].

Although some scholars said: the intended meaning is only what He dispersed of creatures on the earth, so it would be the use of the whole where only a part is meant, which is common in the Qur'an and in the language of the Arabs. And some of them said: the intended meaning of the creatures of the sky are the angels, claiming that crawling (dabib) is applied to every movement.

قال مُقَيِّدُه (ناظم الحواشي) - عفا الله عنه: ظاهر الآية الكريمة أنَّ الله بثَّ في السماء دوابَّ كما بثَّ في (p-261) الأرض دوابَّ. ولا شكَّ أنَّ الله قادرٌ على جمع أهل السماوات وأهل الأرض، وعلى كل شيء، ولكنَّ الآيات القرآنية التي ذكرنا بيَّنت أنَّ المراد بجمعهم حشرهم جميعًا يوم القيامة، وقد أطبق على ذلك المفسِّرون. ولو سلَّمنا تسليمًا جدليًّا أنها تدل على جمعهم في الدنيا، فلا يلزم من ذلك بلوغ أهل الأرض إلى أهل السماء، بل يجوز عقلًا أن ينحدر مَن في السماء إلى مَن في الأرض؛ لأنَّ الهبوط أهون من الصعود. وما يزعمه مَن لا علم عنده بكتاب الله تعالى، من أنَّ قوله - جلَّ وعلا -: ﴿يا معشرَ الجنِّ والإنس إنِ استطعتم أن تنفذوا من أقطار السماوات والأرض فانفذوا لا تنفذون إلا بسلطان﴾ [الرحمن: 33] يشير إلى الوصول إلى السماء، بدعوى أنَّ المراد بالسلطان في الآية هو هذا العلم الحادث الذي من نتائجه الصواريخ والأقمار الصناعية - وإذًا فإنَّ الآية قد تكون فيها الدلالة على أنهم ينفذون بذلك العلم من أقطار السماوات والأرض - مردودٌ من أوجه:

الأول: أنَّ معنى الآية الكريمة هو إعلام الله - جلَّ وعلا - خلقَه أنهم لا محيص لهم ولا مفرَّ عن قضائه ونفوذ مشيئته فيهم، وذلك عندما تحفُّ بهم صفوفُ الملائكة يوم القيامة، فكلما فرُّوا إلى جهة وجدوا صفوف الملائكة أمامهم، ويُقال لهم في ذلك الوقت: ﴿يا معشرَ الجنِّ والإنس﴾ [الرحمن: 33]. والسلطان: قيل الحجة والبينة، وقيل الملك والسلطنة، وكل ذلك معدوم عندهم يوم القيامة، فلا نفوذ لهم، كما قال تعالى: ﴿وجاء ربُّك والملَكُ صفًّا صفًّا﴾ [الفجر: 22]، وقال: ﴿إني أخاف عليكم يومَ التَّنادِ * يومَ تولَّون مدبرين ما لكم من الله من عاصم﴾ [غافر: 32-33].

الوجه الثاني: أنَّ الجنَّ أعطاهم الله القدرة على الطيران والنفوذ في أقطار السماوات والأرض، وكانوا يسترقون السمع من السماء، كما صرَّح به تعالى في قوله عنهم: ﴿وأنا كنا نقعد منها مقاعد للسمع﴾ الآية [الجن: 9]، وإنما مُنعوا من ذلك حين بُعث ﷺ، كما قال تعالى: ﴿فمن يستمع الآن يجد له شهابًا رصدًا﴾ [الجن: 9]. فالجنُّ كانوا قادرين على بلوغ السماء من غير حاجة إلى صاروخ ولا قمر صناعي، فلو كان معنى الآية هو ما يزعمه أولئك الذين لا علم لهم بكتاب الله، لم يقل - جلَّ وعلا -: يا معشر الجن؛ لأنهم كانوا ينفذون إلى السماء قبل حدوث السلطان المزعوم.

الوجه الثالث: أنَّ العلمَ المذكورَ الذي لا يجاوز صناعةً يدويةً أهونُ على الله - جلَّ وعلا - من أن يُطلَق عليه اسمُ السلطان؛ لأنه لا يجاوز أغراض هذه الحياة الدنيا، ولا نظر فيه (p-262) ألبتةَ لما بعد الموت. ولأنَّ الدنيا كلَّها لا تزن عند الله جناحَ بعوضة.

وقد نصَّ تعالى على كمال حقارتها عنده في قوله - جلَّ وعلا -: ﴿ولولا أن يكون الناسُ أمةً واحدةً لجعلنا لمن يكفر بالرحمن لبيوتهم سُقفًا من فضة﴾ إلى قوله ﴿للمتقين﴾ [الزخرف: 33-35]. وعلِم هؤلاء الكفارُ نفيَ الله عنه اسمَ العلم الحقيقي، وأثبت له أنه علمٌ ظاهرٌ من الحياة الدنيا، وذلك في قوله: ﴿وعدَ الله لا يخلف اللهُ وعدَه * ولكنَّ أكثرَ الناس لا يعلمون * يعلمون ظاهرًا من الحياة الدنيا * وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون﴾ [الروم: 6-7]. فحِذْقُ الكفار في الصناعات اليدوية كحذق بعض الحيوانات في صناعتها، بإلهام الله لها ذلك؛ فالنحلُ تبني بيتَ عسلها على صورة شكلٍ مسدَّس، يحار فيه حذّاقُ المهندسين. ولمَّا أرادوا أن يتعلموا منها كيفيةَ ذلك البناء، وجعلوها في أجباحِ زجاجٍ لينظروا إلى كيفية بنائها، أبَتْ أن تعلِّمهم، فطلَتِ الزجاجَ بالعسل قبل البناء، كيلا يروا كيفيةَ بنائها، كما أخبرتنا الثقةُ بذلك.

الوجه الرابع: أنا لو سلَّمنا تسليمًا جدليًّا أن ذلك المعنى المزعومَ كذبًا هو معنى الآية، فإنَّ الله أتبع ذلك بقوله: ﴿يُرسَلُ عليكما شواظٌ من نارٍ﴾ الآية [الرحمن: 35]، فهو يدل على ذلك التقدير على أنهم لو أرادوا النفوذ في أقطارها حرَقهم ذلك الشواظُ والنحاسُ. والشواظُ اللهبُ الخالص، والنحاسُ الدخانُ، ومنه قولُ النابغة:

يُضيءُ كضوءِ سراجِ السَّليطِ ∗∗∗ لم يجعلِ اللهُ فيه نُحاسًا

(يُضيء كضوء سراج الزيت الصافي، لم يجعل الله فيه دخانًا.)

وكذلك ما يزعمه بعضُ مَن لا علم له بمعنى كتاب الله، من أنَّ الله أشار إلى اتصال أهل السماوات وأهل الأرض بقوله تعالى: ﴿قال ربِّي يعلمُ القولَ في السماء والأرض﴾ [الأنبياء: 4] بصيغة الأمر في لفظة (قُلْ) على قراءة الجمهور، وبصيغة الماضي (قالَ ربي يعلم) الآيةَ في قراءة حمزةَ والكسائيِّ وحفصٍ عن عاصم - فإنَّ الآية الكريمة لا تدل على ذلك، لا بدلالة المطابقة ولا التضمن ولا الالتزام؛ لأنَّ غايةَ ما تفيده الآيةُ الكريمةُ أنَّ الله - جلَّ وعلا - أمر نبيَّه أن يقول إنَّ ربَّه يعلم كلَّ ما يقوله أهلُ السماء وأهلُ الأرض، على قراءة الجمهور وعلى قراءة الأخوين وحفص، فمعنى الآية أنه ﷺ أخبر قائلًا إنَّ ربَّه - جلَّ وعلا - يعلم كلَّ ما يُقال في السماء والأرض، وهذا واضح لا إشكال فيه، ولا شكَّ أنه - جلَّ وعلا - عالِمٌ بكلِّ أسرار أهل السماء والأرض وعلانياتهم، لا يعزُب عنه مثقالُ ذرةٍ في السماء ولا في الأرض، ولا أصغرَ من ذلك ولا أكبرَ إلا في كتاب مبين.

وكذلك ما يزعمه مَن لا علم عنده بمعنى كتاب الله - جلَّ وعلا - من أنه تعالى أشار (p-263) إلى أنَّ أهل الأرض سيصعدون إلى السماوات واحدةً بعد أخرى بقوله: ﴿لتركبُنَّ طبقًا عن طبقٍ﴾ [الانشقاق: 19]، زاعمًا أنَّ معنى الآية الكريمة: لتركبُنَّ أيها الناس طبقًا، أي سماءً عن طبق، أي بعد سماء، حتى تصعدوا فوق السماوات، فهو أيضًا جهلٌ بكتاب الله وحملٌ له على غير ما يُراد به.

اعلَمْ أولًا أنَّ في هذا الحرف قراءتين سبعيتين مشهورتين: إحداهما: (لَتَرْكَبَنَّ) بفتح الباء، وبها قرأ من السبعة ابنُ كثير وحمزةُ والكسائيُّ. وعلى هذه القراءة ففي فاعل (لتركبنَّ) ثلاثةُ أوجه معروفة عند العلماء:

الأول، وهو أشهرها: أنَّ الفاعل ضميرُ الخطاب الواقع على النبي ﷺ، أي: لتركبَنَّ أنتَ يا نبيَّ الله طبقًا عن طبقٍ، أي بعد طبقٍ، أي حالًا بعد حالٍ، أي فتترقَّى في الدرجات درجةً بعد درجة. والطبقُ في لغة العرب الحالُ، ومنه قولُ الأقرع بن حابس التميمي:

إنِّي امرؤٌ قد حلبتُ الدهرَ أشطرَه ∗∗∗ وساقني طبقٌ منها إلى طبقِ

(إني رجل قد جرّبتُ شطرَي الدهر، وساقني حال منه إلى حال.)

وقولُ الآخر:

كذلك المرءُ إن يُنسأْ له أجلٌ ∗∗∗ يركبْ على طبقٍ من بعده طبقُ

(كذلك الإنسان إن أُخِّر له أجل، يركب بعد حال حالٌ أخرى.)

أي: حالٌ بعد حالٍ في البيتين. وقال ابنُ مسعودٍ والشعبيُّ ومجاهدٌ وابنُ عباسٍ في إحدى الروايتين والكلبيُّ وغيرُهم: ﴿لتركبُنَّ طبقًا عن طبقٍ﴾ أي: لتصعدنَّ يا محمدُ سماءً بعد سماءٍ، وقد وقع ذلك ليلةَ الإسراء.

والثاني: أنَّ الفاعل ضميرُ السماء، أي: لتركبَنَّ هي، أي السماءُ، طبقًا بعد طبقٍ، أي لتنتقلنَّ السماءُ من حالٍ إلى حال، أي تصير تارةً كالدِّهان، وتارةً كالمُهل، وتارةً تتشقق بالغمام، وتارةً تُطوى كطيِّ السجلِّ للكتب.

والثالث: أنَّ الفاعل ضميرٌ يعود إلى الإنسان المذكور في قوله: ﴿يا أيها الإنسانُ إنك كادحٌ إلى ربِّك كدحًا﴾ [الانشقاق: 6]، أي: لتركبَنَّ أيها الإنسانُ حالًا بعد حالٍ، من صغرٍ إلى كبرٍ، ومن صحةٍ إلى سقمٍ كالعكس، ومن غنًى إلى فقرٍ كالعكس، ومن موتٍ إلى حياةٍ كالعكس، ومن هَولٍ من أهوال القيامة إلى آخرَ، وهكذا.

والقراءة الثانية، وبها قرأ من السبعة نافعٌ وابنُ عامرٍ وأبو عمرٍو وعاصمٌ: (لَتُرْكَبُنَّ) بضم الباء، وهو خطابٌ عامٌّ للناس (p-264) المذكورين في قوله: ﴿فأما مَن أوتي كتابَه بيمينه﴾ إلى قوله ﴿وأما مَن أوتي كتابَه وراءَ ظهرِه﴾ [الانشقاق: 7-10]. ومعنى الآية: لتُرْكَبُنَّ أيها الناسُ حالًا بعد حال، فتنتقلون في دار الدنيا من طَورٍ إلى طور، وفي الآخرة من هولٍ إلى هول.

فإن قيل: يجوز بحسب وضع اللغة العربية التي نزل بها القرآن، على قراءة ضمِّ الباء، أن يكون المعنى: لتُرْكَبُنَّ أيها الناسُ طبقًا بعد طبقٍ، أي سماءً بعد سماء، حتى تصعدوا فوق السماء السابعة، كما تقدم نظيرُه في قراءة فتح الباء خطابًا للنبي ﷺ. وإذا كان هذا جائزًا في لغة القرآن، فما المانعُ من حمل الآية عليه؟ فالجواب من ثلاثة أوجه:

الأول: أنَّ ظاهر القرآن يدل على أنَّ المراد بالطبق الحالُ المنتقَلُ إليها من موتٍ ونحوِه وهولِ القيامة، بدليل قوله بعده مرتِّبًا له عليه بالفاء: ﴿فما لهم لا يؤمنون * وإذا قُرئ عليهم القرآنُ لا يسجدون﴾ [الانشقاق: 20-21]، فهو قرينةٌ ظاهرةٌ على أنَّ المراد: إذا كانوا ينتقلون من حالٍ إلى حال، ومن هولٍ إلى هول، فما المانعُ لهم من أن يؤمنوا ويستعدوا لتلك الشدائد؟ ويؤيده أنَّ العرب تسمي الدواهيَ "بناتِ طَبَق"، كما هو معروف في لغتهم.

الوجه الثاني: أنَّ الصحابةَ - رضي الله عنهم - هم المخاطَبون الأولون بهذا الخطاب، وهم أولى الناس بالدخول فيه بحسب الوضع العربي، ولم يركب أحدٌ منهم سماءً بعد سماءٍ بإجماع المسلمين، فدلَّ ذلك على أنَّ ذلك ليس معنى الآية، ولو كان هو معناها لما خرج منه المخاطَبون الأولون بلا قرينةٍ على ذلك.

The third aspect: it is what we have already mentioned of the Qur'anic verses that explicitly state the preservation and guarding of the heaven from every accursed devil, whoever he may be. From this it becomes clear that the noble verse contains no evidence for the ascent of the operators of artificial satellites above the seven layers. The future will reveal the reality of those lies and baseless claims. The same applies to what some people who have no knowledge of the meaning of the Book of Allah, may He be exalted, claim: that Allah, Exalted is He, indicated the arrival of the people of the earth at the heavens by His saying: ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 13]. They said: His subjecting what is in the heavens to the people of the earth, Exalted is He, is evidence that they will reach the heavens. But the noble verse does not indicate what they claim it indicates, because the Qur'an has explained in many verses how what is in the sky is subjected to the people of the earth. It explained that the subjection of the sun and the moon is for their benefit, the spreading of light over them, and so that they may know the number of years and the reckoning, as He, Exalted, said: ﴿And He subjected to you the sun and the moon, both constant, and He subjected to you the night and the day﴾ [Ibrahim: 33]. The benefits of the sun and the moon, which Allah subjected to the people of the earth, none can count except Allah, as is well known. And He, Exalted, said: ﴿It is He who made the sun a shining light and the moon a light and determined for it phases that you may know the number of years and the reckoning﴾ [Yunus: 5]. And He, Exalted, said: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs, then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible, that you might seek bounty from your Lord and that you might know the number of years and the reckoning﴾ [al-Isra': 12], and other verses that explain this subjection to the people of the earth. Likewise, He subjected the stars to the people of the earth so that they might be guided by them in the darkness of land and sea, as He, Exalted, said: ﴿And the stars are subjected by His command﴾ [al-Nahl: 12], and He, Exalted, said: ﴿And it is He who placed for you the stars that you may be guided by them in the darkness of land and sea﴾ [al-An'am: 97], and He said: ﴿And landmarks; and by the star they are guided﴾ [al-Nahl: 16], and other verses. This, then, is the subjection of what is in the sky to the people of the earth, and the best thing by which the Qur'an is interpreted.

Among what clarifies what we have mentioned is that the first addressees, by His saying ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 13], were the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them. Nothing of what is in the heavens was subjected to them except this subjection we have mentioned, which the mighty Qur'an explained in many verses. So if the alleged subjection through rockets and artificial satellites were intended, the first addressees would have been included in it, as is evident. Likewise His saying: ﴿And how many a sign is there in the heavens and the earth that they pass by while they turn away from it﴾ [Yusuf: 105]. The meaning of their passing by the signs in the heavens is their looking at them, as He, Exalted, explained in many verses:
• such as His saying: ﴿Have they not looked into the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-A'raf: 185];
• and His saying: ﴿Say: Look at what is in the heavens and the earth﴾ [Yunus: 101];
• and His saying: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾ [Fussilat: 53];
and other verses.

Know, may Allah grant success to me and to you, that playing with the Book of Allah, Exalted is He, and interpreting it contrary to its meaning in an attempt to harmonize it with the opinions of the disbelieving Europeans (al-Ifranj), contains absolutely nothing of benefit for this world or the next, but rather it contains the corruption of both abodes. And as we forbid playing with the Book of Allah and interpreting it contrary to its meaning, we urge all Muslims to exert their utmost effort in teaching what benefits them of these worldly sciences while holding fast to their religion, as He, Exalted, said: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power﴾ [al-Anfal: 60], as you will see its elaboration, Allah willing, in the surah of the Children of Israel.

If it is said: These verses by which you have argued for the preservation of the heaven from the devils are concerned with (p. 266) its preservation from eavesdropping, and that is only done by the devils of the jinn; so this indicates that the mentioned verses are restricted to the devils of the jinn. The answer is that the mentioned verses, by their linguistic indication, include the devils of mankind among the disbelievers. Ibn Manzur said in Lisan al-Arab: "The shaytan is well known, and every rebellious transgressor among mankind, jinn, or beasts is a shaytan." And al-Firuzabadi said in al-Qamus: "The shaytan is well known, and every rebellious transgressor from mankind, jinn, or a beast is a shaytan," end of quote.

There is no doubt that among the most rebellious and arrogant disbelievers are those who attempt to reach the heaven, so their inclusion in the name shaytan linguistically is beyond doubt. Since the word shaytan encompasses every rebellious transgressor, His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We guarded it from every accursed devil﴾ [al-Hijr: 17] is explicit in guarding the heaven from every rebellious transgressor, whoever he may be. And interpreting the texts of revelation according to their linguistic meanings is obligatory, unless there is evidence indicating their specification or diverting them from their apparent meaning, as is established in the principles of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh). The guarding of the heaven from the devils means protecting it from them. Al-Jawhari said in his Sihah: "I guarded the thing, guarding it, i.e., I protected it," end of quote. And the author of Lisan al-Arab said: "And I guarded the thing, guarding it, i.e., I protected it," end of quote. This is well known in the speech of the Arabs. So the meaning of this verse by direct indication (dalalat al-mutabaqah) ﴿And We guarded it from every accursed devil﴾ [al-Hijr: 17] is: and We protected it, i.e., the heaven, from every rebellious transgressor.

There is no argument from the opposite (mafhum al-mukhalafah) in His saying "accursed" [al-Hijr: 17] and His saying "rebellious" [al-Saffat: 7], because such attributes are descriptive: every devil is described as accursed and as rebellious, although some of them are more rebellious than others. And whatever Allah, Exalted is He, guarded from every rebellious transgressor, no rebellious transgressor, whoever he may be, can reach it. ﴿Then return the gaze twice; your gaze will return to you humbled while it is fatigued﴾ [al-Mulk: 4]. And knowledge is with Allah, Exalted. End of quote.

His statement, "And We sent the winds fertilizing" (﴿وَأرْسَلْنا الرِّياحَ لَواقِحَ﴾). *Lawaqih* is the plural of *laqih*, and the root meaning of *laqih* is a female that has received the *liqah* (the male's fertilizing contribution) and so has conceived the fetus. From this is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

*"When I say, 'She has become pregnant,' or 'She has begun to conceive,' she has made [the clouds] appear like the primary feathers [of a bird], pregnant or about to conceive."*

The original form of *talaqqah* is *tatalaqqah*, one of the two *ta's* being elided. It means that he imagined she was pregnant, but she was not.

Describing the winds as *lawaqih* is because they are carriers that bear rain, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿until, when they have borne heavy clouds﴾ (Al-A'raf: 57), meaning they carried heavy clouds. So *lawaqih* among camels means those carrying fetuses, and *lawaqih* among winds means those carrying rain. All of them bring good. For this reason a she-camel that does not give birth is called *'aqim* (barren), just as a wind that brings no good is called *'aqim*, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And in 'Ad, when We sent upon them the barren wind﴾ (Adh-Dhariyat: 41), and so on.

Some scholars said: *lawaqih* has the meaning of *malaqih*, i.e., those that fertilize others, such as clouds and trees. On this view there are two possibilities:

First: the intended meaning is attribution (*nisbah*). So His saying *lawaqih* means "possessors of fertilization," just as one says *sa'if* and *ramih*, meaning one who has a sword and a spear. From this is the poet's saying:

*"You deceived me and claimed that you were a milk-giver among the tribe, a date-possessor."*

That is, possessor of milk and dates. On this view the meaning of *lawaqih* is "possessors of fertilization," because they fertilize the clouds and the trees.

The second possibility: *lawaqih* means *malaqih*, the plural of *mulqihah*, and *mulqih* is an active participle, meaning those that impregnate the clouds and trees, as the stallion impregnates the female. The most that can be said for this view is that *lawaqih* is used while *malaqih* is intended. A parallel to this is the saying of Dirar ibn Nahshal, lamenting his brother Yazid or someone else:

*"Let Yazid weep, one humbled by a dispute, and one entangled in what the calamities (ta'iha) overthrow."*

The narration is *tutih*, with a *damma* on the *ta'*, from *atah* (the fourth form). The fitting word would be *al-mutihat*, not *at-tawa'ih*, but the poet used *at-tawa'ih* and intended *al-mutihat*. Likewise it is said here: the word *lawaqih* is used while *malaqih* is intended, that is, *mulqihat* by the active participle form.

The meaning of the winds impregnating the clouds and trees is that Allah makes them the means for these, as the male is for the female. Just as the female conceives through the mating of the stallion, so too the cloud fills with water through the winds stirring it, and the tree bursts forth from its sheaths and leaves through the fertilization of the wind.

Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir of this noble verse, ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾ (Al-Hijr: 22): that is, they fertilize the clouds so that they pour forth water, and they fertilize the trees so that they open up their leaves and sheaths.

As-Suyuti said in *ad-Durr al-Manthur*: "Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, at-Tabarani, and al-Kharaiti in *Makarim al-Akhlaq* transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning His saying ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾, that he said: Allah sends the wind, and it carries water, and it fertilizes the clouds with it, so it pours forth as a milch-camel pours forth, then it rains."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu ash-Shaykh in *al-'Azamah* transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: Allah sends the wind, and it carries water from the cloud, and it stirs the cloud with it, so it pours forth as a milch-camel pours forth.

Abu 'Ubayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾, that he said: it fertilizes the tree and stirs the cloud.

Abu 'Ubayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu ash-Shaykh transmitted from Abu Raja', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I said to al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with him: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾. He said: fertilizing for the trees. I said: or the clouds? He said: and for the clouds, you pass by them until they rain.

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Qatadah concerning His saying ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾, that he said: it fertilizes the water in the cloud.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from ad-Dahhak concerning His saying ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾, that he said: the wind that Allah sends upon the cloud fertilizes it, so it fills with water.

Ibn Abi ad-Dunya in *Kitab as-Sahab*, Ibn Jarir, Abu ash-Shaykh in *al-'Azamah*, Ibn Mardawayh, and ad-Daylami in *Musnad al-Firdaws*, with a weak chain, transmitted from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The south wind is from Paradise." It is the fertilizing wind that Allah mentioned in His Book, and in it are benefits for people. The north wind is from Hell; it comes forth and passes by Paradise, and a breath from it reaches Paradise, and this is its coolness.

Ibn Abi ad-Dunya transmitted from Qatadah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was given victory by the east wind (as-saba), the people of 'Ad were destroyed by the west wind (ad-dabur), and the south wind is from Paradise, and it is the fertilizing wind."

This is the summary of the scholars' meaning concerning the fertilizing winds. We have already mentioned the view of one who said that the *lawaqih* are the carriers of rain, and that this view is supported by His saying: ﴿until, when they have borne heavy clouds﴾, meaning they carried them. In the introduction to this blessed book we previously mentioned that among the types of clarification (bayan) it contains is that a thing has attributes, some of which are mentioned in one place, and we then clarify the rest of those attributes mentioned in other places. We gave as an example the shade of the people of Paradise, for He described it in Surat an-Nisa' as *zalil* (dense) in His saying: ﴿And We shall admit them into dense shade﴾ (An-Nisa': 57). He described it with other attributes in other places. We have explained the attributes of the shade of the people of Paradise mentioned in other than that place, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Its food is everlasting, and its shade﴾ (Ar-Ra'd: 35).
• And His saying: ﴿and extended shade﴾ (Al-Waqi'ah: 30), and other of its attributes.

Knowing this, understand that He, exalted is He, described the winds in this verse by their being *lawaqih*, and we have explained the meaning of that just now. He described them in other places with other attributes. Among these is His describing them as bringers of good tidings of the clouds, in His saying: ﴿And among His signs is that He sends the winds as bearers of good tidings﴾ (Ar-Rum: 46).

• And His saying: ﴿And He it is who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy﴾ according to the reading of one who reads it with *ba'* (*bushran*).

Among these is His describing them as stirring up the clouds, such as His saying: ﴿Allah is He who sends the winds so they stir up clouds﴾ (Al-Furqan: 48), and the rest of the verse.

The author of *ad-Durr al-Manthur* said: Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu ash-Shaykh in *al-'Azamah* transmitted from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, who said: "Allah sends the *muthirah* (stirring wind), and it sweeps the earth clean, then He sends the *mubashshirah* (bearer of glad tidings), and it stirs the cloud, and He makes it fragments (*kisaf*), then He sends the *mu'allifah* (gathering wind), and it gathers it together, and He makes it heaped up (*rukam*), then He sends the *lawaqih*, and they fertilize it, so it rains."

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn 'Umayr, who said: "The winds are four: a wind that sweeps clean, a wind that stirs and makes it fragments, a wind that makes it heaped up, and a wind that brings rain." End of quotation.

Issues related to this noble verse:

The first issue: Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, took from this noble verse that the fertilization of wheat is that it becomes *yuhabbib* (forms its grains) and *yusanbil* (forms its ears). Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir of this noble verse: Ibn Wahb, Ibn al-Qasim, Ashhab, and Ibn 'Abd al-Hakam transmitted from Malik, and the wording is Ashhab's:

Malik said: Allah, exalted is He, said ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾ (Al-Hijr: 22). So the fertilization of wheat, in my view, is that it forms its grains and forms its ears. I do not know what dries up in its sheaths, but it forms grains until, if it dried, it would not be corrupted, having no good in it. The fertilization of all trees is that they bear fruit, then some of it falls and some of it stays, and that is not by being *yuwarrad* (made to flower).

Ibn al-'Arabi said: Malik relied in this explanation on comparing the fertilization of trees to the fertilization of pregnancy, and that when the child is formed, shaped, and the spirit is breathed into it, it is like the forming of grains in fruit and its ear forming, because it is named by a name in which every pregnant female shares. On this the hadith came: "The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade selling *hibb* until it hardens." End of quotation from al-Qurtubi.

The author of these notes, may Allah pardon him, says: Imam Malik's derivation from this verse, that the fertilization of wheat is that it forms grains and forms ears, and Ibn al-'Arabi's evidence for it from the mentioned hadith, are not, in my view, entirely clear.

The second issue: Know that the fertilization (*ta'bir*) of fruits is *ibar*, which is that some of the male date palm's pollen (*tal'*) is taken and placed among the female spathes. The meaning of this for the rest of fruits is the emergence of fruits such as figs and others, until the fruit becomes visible and observed. According to Malik and his companions, what is considered for fruits that are masculinized (i.e., have male pollination) is the masculinization, and for those not so, that some of their blossom remains and what falls falls. The limit of this for grain is its emergence from the earth, as Malik said. It is also narrated from him that its *ibar* is that it forms grains. End of quotation from al-Qurtubi. He also said: Scholars have not disagreed that if an orchard's female spathes have split open and their *ibar* has been delayed, while others of similar condition have been pollinated, its ruling is the ruling of what has been pollinated. If part of the orchard has been pollinated, what has not been pollinated follows it, just as when the good condition of part of an orchard appears, the whole orchard follows that ripeness in permissibility of its sale. End of quotation. Further clarification of this will come, Allah willing.

The third issue: If an orchard of date palms is sold after it has been pollinated, its fruit belongs to the seller unless the buyer stipulates it. If the buyer stipulates it, it is his. The evidence for this is the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "Whoever buys date palms after they have been pollinated, their fruit belongs to the seller who sold them, unless the buyer stipulates it," agreed upon, from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them.

If date palms are sold before pollination, the fruit belongs to the buyer. There is disagreement over the seller's exception of it. The well-known position of Malik's school is that it is like the fetus: it is not permissible for the seller to stipulate it or to except it, based on the view that the excepted item is a purchased item. In contrast, al-Lakhmi's preferred opinion permits the seller's exception of it, based on the view that the excepted item is retained by the seller. The permissibility of excepting it is the position of ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Abu Hanifah, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on them.

He (the author, may Allah pardon him) said: This is more apparent to me, because the excepted fruit remaining with the seller is more apparent than its being bought, since it was the seller's property and has remained in his ownership, as the sale did not include it because it was excepted from the whole of what was sold, as you can see. What we have mentioned in this question is the truth, God willing: fruit that has been pollinated (*ta'bir*, the fertilising of date palms by dusting them with pollen) belongs to the seller unless a condition is stipulated otherwise, and fruit that has not been pollinated belongs to the buyer unless a condition is stipulated otherwise. This differs from the view of Ibn Abi Layla, who said: it belongs to the buyer in both cases, because it is attached to the trunk by a natural connection and so follows it, like the branches. This argument is invalid in its reasoning, because it contradicts the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim, which was mentioned just above, in which the Prophet ﷺ explicitly stated that if the sale took place after pollination, the fruit belongs to the seller. It also differs from the view of Imam Abu Hanifa and al-Awza'i, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on them both, who said that it belongs to the seller in both cases. The hadith mentioned refutes them both, by its implied meaning, that is, the inference by contrast (*mafhum al-mukhalafa*): the Prophet's ﷺ saying, "Whoever buys a date palm that has been pollinated..." (the hadith), implies that if the fruit has not been pollinated, the ruling is not the same. Otherwise, his saying "that has been pollinated" and his saying in some narrations "after it has been pollinated" would be meaningless and without benefit. It is therefore established that mention of the attribute of pollination is to exclude other cases. It is known that Imam Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, does not accept inference by contrast as proof. Therefore, according to his principles, the Prophet ﷺ in the mentioned hadith stated the ruling for pollinated fruit and remained silent about non-pollinated fruit, so he did not address it at all.

If some of the fruit of the sold palms has been pollinated and some has not, the position of Malik is that if one of the two is more numerous, the lesser follows it; if they are equal, each has its own ruling: the pollinated fruit belongs to the seller and the rest to the buyer. The position of Imam Ahmad is that each of the pollinated and non-pollinated fruit has its own ruling. Abu Hanifa makes no distinction between pollinated and non-pollinated fruit; all of it belongs to the seller unless the buyer stipulates otherwise. The position of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, which is the sound view among the differing opinions, is that what has not been pollinated follows what has been pollinated (p. 271), so all of it remains with the seller, to avoid the harm of having different hands (owners) in control.

Know that excepting some of the fruit but not all of it is permissible according to the view of the majority of scholars, in agreement with Ashhab among the companions of Malik. Ibn al-Qasim disagreed and said: it is not permissible to except part of the pollinated fruit. The majority's proof is that whatever it is permissible to except in its entirety, it is permissible to except in part. Ibn al-Qasim's proof is that the text was only given regarding stipulating the whole.

Know that most scholars hold that the pollinated fruit, which belongs to the seller if the buyer has not excepted it, remains until the time of its customary use, and the buyer is not required to cut it immediately. This is the view of Malik, al-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Abu Hanifa disagreed, saying: it is obligatory to cut it immediately and to clear the palm of it, because it is a sold item occupied by the seller's property, so it is obligatory to remove it and clear it, just as if he had sold a house containing food or cloth belonging to him. The majority argue that removing and clearing the sold item is according to custom and usual practice, just as if he sold a house containing food, its removal is not obligatory according to the usual practice in that regard, which is that he removes it by day, bit by bit, and he is not obliged to remove it at night, nor to gather the animals of the town to carry it. Likewise here, the palm is cleared of its fruit at the appropriate time, which is the time of harvesting. This was stated by Ibn Qudama in *al-Mughni*.

Fourth issue: If the palm trees are bought while the fruit remains with the seller, may the buyer of the trunks (the palms) buy the fruit before it has ripened? First: scholars differ on this. The well-known position of Malik is that this is permissible, because in his view the fruit has the status of a subordinate even when it is separately contracted. In another narration from him, it is not permissible. The Shafi'is and Hanbalis have two views, one prohibiting and one permitting. Ibn Qudama said in *al-Mughni*: al-Qurtubi attributed to al-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifa, al-Thawri, the people of the literal interpretation (*Ahl al-Zahir*) and the jurists of hadith the view of prohibiting this, then said: and it is the more apparent of the hadiths prohibiting the sale of fruit before it has ripened.

Fifth issue: If the fruit alone is bought without the palm trees, before it has ripened, there are three cases. The first: he sells it on condition that it remains on the tree until the time of harvesting; in this case the sale is invalid by consensus. The second: he sells it on condition that it is cut immediately; in this case the sale is valid by consensus. The third: he sells it without a condition of leaving it or cutting it, but they remain silent about that and conclude the sale in unrestricted form without a condition. In this case, the sale is not valid according to the majority of scholars, including Malik, al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on them all. Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, permitted the sale in this case and required the fruit to be cut immediately. He said: because an unrestricted contract requires cutting, so it is as if he had stipulated it. The majority's proof is the general application of the texts transmitted from him ﷺ on this matter. Among them is what al-Bukhari and Muslim (p. 272), Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah transmitted from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of fruits until their ripening becomes apparent," he forbade the seller and the buyer. In another wording: "He forbade the sale of date palms until they turn red (*tazhu*), and the sale of ears of grain until they whiten and are safe from blight." Narrated by Imam Ahmad, Muslim and the authors of the Sunan, except Ibn Majah. Among them is what al-Bukhari and Muslim transmitted in their Sahihs from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of fruits until they turn red (*tuzhi*)." It was said: "What is its reddening?" He said: "It turns red and yellow." Among them also is what Ahmad, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not trade fruits until their ripening becomes apparent." Among them is what Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim narrated, and both of them authenticated, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that "the Prophet ﷺ forbade the sale of grapes until they turn black, and the sale of grain until it hardens."

The unrestricted wording of these texts and similar ones indicates the prohibition of selling fruit before its ripening in the case of an unrestricted sale with no condition, as has been explained above.

The majority of the reciters read this noble verse, "And We send the winds" (﴿وَأرْسَلْنا الرِّياحَ﴾), in the plural form. Hamza read "And We send the wind" (*wa-arsalna al-rih*) in the singular, and the alif in Hamza's reading denotes the genus. Therefore the plural is valid in His saying "fertilising" (*lawaqih*). Abu Hayyan said in *al-Bahr al-Muhit*: whoever reads the wind in the singular does so according to the interpretation of the genus, as they say, "The yellow dinar has destroyed people, and the white dirham," end of quote. And knowledge is with Allah the Exalted.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: "Then We sent down water from the sky and made you drink of it" (﴿فَأنْزَلْنا مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَأسْقَيْناكُمُوهُ﴾). In this noble verse He, exalted, explained His great favour in sending down water from the sky and making it sweet and fit for drinking. He explained this also in other places, such as His saying: "Have you considered the water which you drink? Is it you who sent it down from the cloud, or are We the sender? Had We willed, We could have made it bitter; then why do you not give thanks?" (﴿أفَرَأيْتُمُ الماءَ الَّذِي تَشْرَبُونَ﴾ ﴿أأنْتُمْ أنْزَلْتُمُوهُ مِنَ المُزْنِ أمْ نَحْنُ المُنْزِلُونَ﴾ ﴿لَوْ نَشاءُ جَعَلْناهُ أُجاجًا فَلَوْلا تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 68–70]). And His saying: "It is He who sent down water from the sky; from it you have drink, and from it grows the vegetation in which you pasture your livestock. With it He grows for you crops, olives, date palms, grapes and every kind of fruit" (﴿هُوَ الَّذِي أنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً لَكم مِنهُ شَرابٌ ومِنهُ شَجَرٌ فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ﴾ ﴿يُنْبِتُ لَكم بِهِ الزَّرْعَ والزَّيْتُونَ والنَّخِيلَ والأعْنابَ ومِن كُلِّ الثَّمَراتِ﴾ [al-Nahl: 10–11]). And His saying: "And We sent down from the sky pure water, to give life thereby to a dead land, and to give drink to what We have created of cattle and many people" (﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً طَهُورًا لِنُحْيِيَ بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَيْتًا﴾ ﴿وَنُسْقِيَهُ مِمّا خَلَقْنا أنْعامًا وأناسِيَّ كَثِيرًا﴾ [al-Furqan: 48–49]), and other verses besides these.

The verified position is that *asqa* and *saqa* are two dialectal forms with the same meaning, like *asra* and *sara*. The evidence for this is the two canonical readings of His saying: "And indeed in the cattle there is a lesson for you: We give you to drink of what is in their bellies" (﴿وَإنَّ لَكم في الأنْعامِ لَعِبْرَةً نُسْقِيكم مِمّا في بُطُونِهِ﴾ [al-Nahl: 66]). Some of the Seven read it with a *damma* on the *nun* from the quadriliteral *asqa*, and some read it with a *fatha* from the triliteral *saqa*. This is also shown by the verse of Labid:

"He gave drink to my people, the Banu Majd, and gave drink to Numayr and the tribes of Hilal."

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: "And you are not its keepers" (﴿وَما أنْتُمْ لَهُ بِخازِنِينَ﴾).

On this, the scholars have two interpretations, both of which are supported by the Qur'an. The first: the meaning of "and you are not its keepers" (al-Hijr: 22) is that its treasuries are not with you; rather, We are its keepers, sending it down whenever We will. This interpretation is indicated by verses such as His saying: "There is nothing but that its treasuries are with Us, and We send it down only in a known measure" (﴿وَإنْ مِن شَيْءٍ إلّا عِنْدَنا خَزائِنُهُ وما نُنَزِّلُهُ إلّا بِقَدَرٍ مَعْلُومٍ﴾ [al-Hijr: 21]), and His saying: "And to Allah belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth" (﴿وَلِلَّهِ خَزائِنُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾) — the verse [al-Munafiqun: 7] — and other verses of this kind. The second interpretation: the meaning of "and you are not its keepers" is that, after We have sent it down upon you, you are not able to preserve it in wells, springs and pools; rather, We are the ones who preserve it in them, so that it may be a store for you at times of need. This interpretation is supported by His saying: "And We sent down water from the sky in measure, and We caused it to settle in the earth, and indeed We are able to take it away" (﴿وَأنْزَلْنا مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً بِقَدَرٍ فَأسْكَنّاهُ في الأرْضِ وإنّا عَلى ذَهابٍ بِهِ لَقادِرُونَ﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 18]), and His saying: "Say: Have you considered, if your water should sink into the earth, who then will bring you flowing water?" (﴿قُلْ أرَأيْتُمْ إنْ أصْبَحَ ماؤُكم غَوْرًا فَمَن يَأْتِيكم بِماءٍ مَعِينٍ﴾ [al-Mulk: 30]), and His saying: "Or its water sinks away, and you will never be able to find it" (﴿أوْ يُصْبِحَ ماؤُها غَوْرًا فَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعَ لَهُ طَلَبًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 41]), and His saying: "Have you not seen that Allah sent down water from the sky and made it flow in springs in the earth?" (﴿ألَمْ تَرَ أنَّ اللَّهَ أنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَسَلَكَهُ يَنابِيعَ في الأرْضِ﴾ [al-Zumar: 21]), and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 23:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death﴾.

In this noble verse He makes clear that it is He who gives life and causes death, and He has explained this in many verses, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and to Us is the final return﴾ [Qaf: 43].

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿My Lord is He who gives life and causes death﴾ [al-Baqarah: 258].

• And His saying: ﴿There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death, your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers﴾ [al-Dukhan: 8]. And He has made clear in other places that He gave them life twice and caused them to die twice, such as:

• His saying: ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice"﴾ [Ghafir: 11].

• And His saying: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah while you were dead and He gave you life; then He will cause you to die; then He will give you life again﴾ (the verse) [al-Baqarah: 28].

The first causing of death is their state as drops of sperm, clots of blood, and lumps of flesh; the second causing of death is their death when their terms in this world come to an end. The first giving of life is the breathing of the soul into them and their being brought forth alive from the wombs of their mothers; the second giving of life is their being resurrected from their graves alive on the Day of Resurrection. Further clarification of this will come, Allah willing, may He be exalted.
