(p-274) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We are the inheritors﴾.

In this noble verse He, may He be exalted, makes clear that He is the Inheritor, and He does not specify the thing that He inherits. He has explained in other places that He inherits the earth and whoever is upon it, such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, We inherit the earth and whoever is upon it, and to Us they will be returned﴾ [Maryam: 40], and His saying: ﴿And We will inherit from him what he says, and he will come to Us alone﴾ [Maryam: 80]. The meaning of "what he says" is: We will inherit from him that which he claims he will be given on the Day of Resurrection of wealth and children, as Allah mentioned about him in His saying: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"?﴾ [Maryam: 77]. The meaning of His inheriting the earth and whoever is upon it is that He remains after the annihilation of His creation, characterized by the attributes of perfection and majesty, doing whatever He wills in whatever manner He wills.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 26:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We did certainly create man from clay of altered black mud, molded.﴾

In this noble verse, He, exalted is He, makes clear that He created our father Adam from ṣalṣāl (dry clay) of ḥama' (altered black mud) masnūn (molded). Ṣalṣāl is dry clay that gives forth a ringing sound from its dryness when struck by something, as long as fire has not touched it; once fire touches it, it becomes fakhkhār (potsherd-ware). The root of ṣalīl (a ringing sound) and ṣalṣala (a rattling sound) is one, and the difference between them is that if you perceive in the sound a prolonged note, it is ṣalīl, and if you perceive in it a repeated vibration, it is ṣalṣala. Ḥama' is black, altered mud. As for masnūn, it has been said: shaped, formed from sannat al-wajh, which is its form (ṣūrah). From this is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

"It shows you the sanna of a face, not blemished, smooth, with no mole or scar in it."

It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that when Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq asked him about the meaning of masnūn, and he answered that its meaning is "shaped," he said to him: "Do the Arabs know that?" Ibn ʿAbbās said to him: "Yes. Have you not heard the saying of Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, may Allah be pleased with him, when he was praising the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

"Radiant, as if the full moon were the sanna of his face, the clouds withdrew from him, his light shone forth and spread out."

It has also been said that masnūn means poured, cast, i.e., the form of a human was poured out as images are cast from molten jewels in their moulds. It has been said that masnūn means foul-smelling. Some scholars said: masnūn means smooth. He said: From this is the saying of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥassān: "Then her flank, toward the green dome, walks on masnūn marble," i.e., smooth and polished. This was stated by Ibn Kathir. Mujahid said: ṣalṣāl is that which is foul-smelling. What we have mentioned is the truth, by the evidence of His saying: ﴿He created man from clay like pottery﴾ [al-Rahman: 14]. Having understood this, know that Allah, majestic and exalted, has clarified in His Book the stages (aṭwār) of this clay from which He created Adam. He explained that it was first dust:

• by His saying: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus to Allah is like the likeness of Adam; He created him from dust﴾ [Ali ʿImran: 59],

• and His saying: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, indeed We created you from dust﴾ [al-Hajj: 5],

• and His saying: ﴿It is He who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop﴾ [Ghafir: 67], and other verses. Then He indicated that this dust was moistened and became clay that clings to the hands, in other places,

• such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, We created them from clay that sticks﴾ [al-Saffat: 11],

• and His saying: ﴿And We did certainly create man from an extract of clay﴾ [al-Muminun: 12],

• and His saying: ﴿And He began the creation of man from clay﴾ [al-Sajdah: 7], and other verses. He explained that this clay was black and altered,

• by His saying here: ﴿from altered black mud, molded﴾. He also explained that it dried until it became ṣalṣāl, meaning you hear from it a ringing sound due to its dryness,

• by His saying: ﴿And We did certainly create man from ṣalṣāl﴾, the verse [al-Hijr: 26],

• and His saying: ﴿He created man from ṣalṣāl like pottery﴾, the verse [al-Rahman: 14].

And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Hijr

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We did certainly create man from ṣalṣāl from ḥama' masnūn.﴾

The apparent meaning of this verse is that Adam was created from ṣalṣāl, i.e., dry clay.

Other verses have come indicating otherwise, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿from clay that sticks﴾ [al-Saffat: 11], and His saying: ﴿the likeness of Adam; He created him from dust﴾ [Ali ʿImran: 59].

The answer is that He mentioned the stages (aṭwār) of that dust: He mentioned its first stage by His saying: ﴿from dust﴾, then it was moistened and became sticky clay, then it was left to ferment and became ḥama' masnūn, then it dried and became ṣalṣāl like pottery.

This is clear, and knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 31:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Except Iblis; he refused to be among those who prostrate﴾. In this noble verse He made clear that Iblis refused to prostrate to Adam. In other places He made clear that he was arrogant towards carrying out the command of his Lord, such as His saying in al-Baqarah: ﴿Except Iblis; he refused and was arrogant﴾ [al-Baqarah: 34], the verse in full, and His saying in Sad: ﴿Except Iblis; he was arrogant and was among the disbelievers﴾ [Sad: 74]. He alluded to this here with His saying: ﴿He said: I would not prostrate to a human whom You created from clay, from black mud altered﴾ [al-Hijr: 33]. As was previously indicated.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 32:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿He said, "O Iblis, what is [the matter] with you that you are not among those who prostrate?"﴾ In this noble verse, Allah, may He be exalted, makes clear that He asked Iblis a question of reproach and rebuke about the reason for his refusal to prostrate to Adam, which his Lord, may He be exalted and high, had commanded him to do. He also makes clear in al-A'raf and Sad that He likewise rebuked him with this question. In al-A'raf He said, ﴿He said, "What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 12], and in Sad He said: ﴿He said, "O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My two hands?"﴾ and so on [Sad: 75]. He called him by his name, Iblis, in al-Hijr and Sad, and did not call him by it in al-A'raf.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 33:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "I would never prostrate myself to a human whom You created from clay, from black mud, molded."﴾

This statement which He, exalted and most high, mentioned in this noble verse, on the part of Iblis, may Allah curse him, that he would not prostrate to a human created from clay, is intended to mean that he is better than Adam, because Adam was created from clay while he was created from fire, as His statement, exalted is He, clarifies: ﴿He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."﴾ [Sad: 76].

(p-276) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Then get out of it, for indeed you are accursed."﴾

In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted explains that He commanded Iblis (Satan) to leave the Garden, emphasizing that he is accursed (rajim). In al-A'raf He explained that this was an exit of descent (khuruj hubut), and that he would leave characterized by abasement, humiliation, and disgrace, by His saying: ﴿He said, "Then descend from it. It is not for you to be arrogant therein, so get out. Indeed, you are among the debased."﴾ [al-A'raf: 13].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 35:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense﴾. In this noble verse He made clear that the curse is upon Iblis until the Day of Recompense, and He stated explicitly in Surah Sad that His curse, exalted is He, is upon Iblis until the Day of Recompense, by His saying: ﴿And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense﴾ [Sad: 78]. We have already explained the Day of Recompense (yawm al-din) in al-Fatihah.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 39:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿He said: "My Lord, because You have led me astray...﴾ the verse. Some of the scholars said: this is an oath by Iblis by the leading-astray of Allah for him, on the basis that he will lead the children of Adam astray, except for the sincere servants of Allah. What supports this is that he swore by His might, may He be exalted, concerning that in His saying: ﴿He said: "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all"﴾ [Sad: 82], the verse. It has also been said: the "ba'" (preposition "bi," here meaning "because of") in His saying ﴿because You have led me astray﴾ [al-Hijr: 39] is causal (sababiyyah).

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿I will surely make [evil] appealing to them on earth and will surely mislead them all﴾.

In this noble verse, He, may He be exalted, mentioned that Iblis informed that he would exert his effort in misguiding the children of Adam until he misguides most of them. He clarified this meaning in other places:

• Such as His saying: ﴿I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path. Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left. And You will not find most of them grateful﴾ [al-A'raf: 16–17].

• And His saying: ﴿And he said, "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion"﴾ the verse [al-Nisa': 118].

• And His saying: ﴿He said, "Have You considered this one whom You have honored above me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize his descendants, except for a few"﴾ [al-Isra': 62]. Iblis said this before it occurred, by way of supposition on his part that he would be able to mislead most of the children of Adam. Allah has clarified that his supposition came true,

• by His saying: ﴿And Iblis had already confirmed his assumption about them, so they followed him, except for a party of the believers﴾ [Saba': 20]. Every verse in which the misguiding of the children of Adam by Iblis is mentioned clarifies that Iblis and all who followed him are in the Fire, as He said here: ﴿And indeed, Hell is the promised place for them all. It has seven gates﴾ [al-Hijr: 43–44], the verse. He said in al-A'raf: ﴿He said, "Get out of it, despised and expelled. Whoever follows you among them – I will surely fill Hell with you all"﴾ [al-A'raf: 18]. He said in Surat Bani Isra'il: ﴿He said, "Go, and whoever follows you among them – indeed, Hell is your recompense, an ample recompense"﴾ [al-Isra': 63]. He said in Sad: ﴿He said, "So the truth I say, and the truth I speak: I will surely fill Hell with you and with whoever follows you among them, all together"﴾ [Sad: 84–85].

(p-277) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿except Your sincere servants among them﴾.

In this noble verse, He, may He be exalted, mentions that when Satan threatened that he would mislead most of the children of Adam, he excepted from that the sincere servants of Allah, acknowledging that he has no power over misleading them. Its parallel is His saying in Surah Sad as well: he said ﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them﴾ [Sad: 82–83]. The sincere servants of Allah are the ones intended by the exception in His saying concerning the Children of Israel: ﴿I will surely seize his descendants, except for a few﴾ [al-Isra: 62], and His saying in Saba': ﴿And Iblis had already confirmed his assumption about them, so they followed him, except for a group of the believers﴾ [Saba: 20]. These are the ones he excluded by His saying ﴿and You will not find most of them grateful﴾ [al-A'raf: 17]. And He, may He be exalted, clarified in other places that Satan has no authority over those sincere servants, such as His saying ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them﴾ [al-Hijr: 42] and ... (the verse continues), and His saying: ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord. His authority is only over those who take him as an ally﴾ [al-Nahl: 99–100], and His saying ﴿And he had no authority over them, except that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter from who is in doubt about it﴾ (the verse continues) [Saba: 21], and His saying: ﴿And I had no authority over you, except that I invited you and you responded to me﴾ [Ibrahim: 22], and His saying: al-mukhlisin [al-Hijr: 40].

Ibn 'Amir, Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read it with a kasra on the lam (ism fa'il, the active participle, "the sincere ones"), while Nafi' and the Kufans read it with a fatha on the lam in the form of ism maf'ul (the passive participle, "those chosen/purified").

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and springs﴾ ﴿Enter them in peace, secure﴾.

In this noble verse He explains that the righteous, on the Day of Resurrection, will be in gardens and springs, and it will be said to them on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Enter them in peace, secure﴾. In other places He mentions the attributes of their reward, and sometimes He explains some of their piety by which they attained this great reward.

Like His words in Adh-Dhariyat: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and springs﴾ ﴿Taking what their Lord has given them. Indeed, they were before that doers of good﴾ ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾ ﴿And before dawn they would ask forgiveness﴾ ﴿And in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 15-19].

And His words in Ad-Dukhan: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure place﴾ ﴿In gardens and springs﴾ ﴿Wearing of fine silk and brocade, facing one another﴾ ﴿Thus, and We will marry them to fair women with large, beautiful eyes﴾ ﴿They will call therein for every fruit, in security﴾ ﴿They will not taste therein death, except the first death. And He will protect them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾ ﴿As a bounty from your Lord. That is the great triumph﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 51-57].

And His words in At-Tur: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and pleasure﴾ ﴿Enjoying what their Lord has given them, and their Lord protected them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾ ﴿Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you used to do﴾ ﴿Reclining on thrones arranged in rows, and We will marry them to fair women with large, beautiful eyes﴾ [At-Tur: 17-20].

And His words in Al-Qamar: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and a river﴾ ﴿In a seat of truth, in the presence of a Sovereign, Omnipotent﴾ [Al-Qamar: 54-55]. And His words in Al-Mursalat: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be among shade and springs﴾ ﴿And fruits of what they desire﴾ ﴿Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you used to do﴾ [Al-Mursalat: 41-43], and other verses besides these.

We have already explained, in the translation of this blessed Book, that among the kinds of exposition it contains is that a thing which has multiple attributes in the Qur'an, we explain its attributes when mentioning some of them, as its example has been mentioned repeatedly before, and as here.

Al-Muttaqi (the righteous) is the active participle of al-ittiqa' (guarding oneself, taking precaution). The root of the verb al-ittiqa' is (w-q-y), a defective-and-hollow-mixed root (lafif mafruq) whose first radical is waw, middle radical is qaf, and last radical is ya'. The infix of the reflexive form (ta' al-ifti'al, the reflexive t-infix) entered it, so it became wiqiya or tiqiya. The waw that is the first radical of the word was then changed into ta' according to the established rule in morphology (al-tasrif): every waw that is the first radical of a word, when the ta' of ifti'al is prefixed to it, must be changed—I mean the waw—into ta' and assimilated into the ta' of ifti'al, as in ittasala from al-wasl, ittazana from al-wazn, ittahada from al-wahda, and ittaqa from al-wiqaya. Ibn Malik set down this rule in al-Khulasa with his words:

"The soft-letter-initial waw or ya' in the ifti'al form is changed; it is rare in the initial hamza case, as in ai-takala."

Al-ittiqa' linguistically means taking a protection against what is disliked. From it is the saying of Nabigha Dhubyani:

"The veil fell, and she did not intend to drop it, so she took it up and shielded us with her hand."

That is, she met us with her hand, making it a protection that screens her from our looking at her face, since she hides it with it. And the saying of another:

"She let fall a veil, behind which the sun was; she shielded herself with the finest of two joined things, a palm and a wrist."

In the technical usage of the Shari'a, taqwa is taking a protection against the punishment of Allah and His wrath, and it is composed of two matters: carrying out the command of Allah, and avoiding His prohibition.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 47:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts, [as] brothers﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted explains that He removes from the people of Paradise whatever resentment is in their breasts, while they are brothers. He explained this meaning in Surat al-A'raf, adding that rivers flow beneath them in the bliss of Paradise. This is in His words: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts; beneath them rivers will flow. And they will say, "Praise be to Allah, who has guided us to this."﴾ [al-A'raf: 43].

* *

(p-279) The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿upon thrones, facing each other﴾.

In this noble verse, He explains that the God-fearing, who are the people of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection, will be upon thrones, and that they will be facing one another, each looking at the face of the other. He described their thrones with beautiful attributes in other places, among them that they are woven with rods of gold (qudban al-dhahab), and that they are arranged (al-mawdu'ah). He said in al-Waqi'ah: ﴿A multitude from the earlier peoples, and a few from the later ones, upon thrones woven [with gold], reclining on them, facing each other﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 13–16]. It was said: al-mawdunah (woven) means al-masfufah (arranged),

• like His words: ﴿reclining upon thrones arranged in rows﴾ [al-Tur: 20]. Among them also that they are raised high,

• like His words in al-Ghashiyah: ﴿therein are thrones raised high﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 13],

• and His words in al-Waqi'ah: ﴿and raised couches﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 34],

• and His words: ﴿reclining upon green cushions and beautiful carpets﴾ [al-Rahman: 76],

and other verses besides these.

**Al-Shinqiti's commentary (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 15, verse 48:**

Allah's words: ﴿They will not be touched therein by any fatigue﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah explains that the people of Paradise will not be touched therein by *nasab* (fatigue), which is weariness and exhaustion. The word *nasab* is an indefinite noun (nakirah) in a negative context, so it is general and covers every kind of fatigue. The verse thus indicates that the people of Paradise are safe from all forms of weariness and hardship. Allah affirmed this same meaning in His words: ﴿Who has settled us in the abode of permanence by His bounty; no fatigue touches us therein, nor does weariness touch us therein﴾ [Fatir: 35], because *lughub* (weariness, exhaustion) is also fatigue and exhaustion. And it is authentically reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed Allah commanded me to give Khadijah the glad tidings of a house in Paradise made of qasab (hollow pearl), with no clamor (sakhab) therein and no fatigue (nasab)."

* *

Allah's words: ﴿Nor will they ever be removed from it﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah explains that the people of Paradise will not leave it. He emphasized the negation of their being removed from it by the particle *bi-* in His words *bi-mukhrajin* (removed), so they will abide in its bliss forever, without cessation. He clarified this meaning in other passages, such as:

• His words: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them will be the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging, abiding therein forever, desiring no change therefrom﴾ [al-Kahf: 107–108]

• His words: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a great reward, remaining therein forever﴾ [al-Kahf: 2–3]

• His words: ﴿A gift uninterrupted﴾ [Hud: 108]

• His words: ﴿Indeed, this is Our provision, which will never end﴾ [Sad: 54]

And other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 51:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And inform them about the guests of Ibrahim﴾.

He made clear in other passages that the guests of Ibrahim mentioned in this verse were angels, as in His saying in Hud: ﴿And certainly Our messengers came to Ibrahim with good tidings. They said, "Peace." He said, "Peace," and he did not delay before bringing a roasted calf﴾ [Hud: 69], as has already passed, and His saying: ﴿He said, "What is your business, O messengers?" They said, "We have been sent to a guilty people"﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 31-32], (p-280) and other verses besides these.

The Qur'an, in this noble verse, does not state whether Ibrahim (peace be upon him) returned the greeting to the angels or not, because it does not mention his returning their greeting. It only says that he said to them, ﴿Indeed, we are fearful of you﴾. It makes clear in Hud and in al-Dhariyat that he did return their greeting. In Hud he said, ﴿Peace,﴾ and ﴿did not delay before bringing a roasted calf﴾ [verse 69].

And in al-Dhariyat, his saying: ﴿He said, "Peace, a people unknown,"﴾ and ﴿So he turned to his family and brought a fat calf﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 25–26]. It also makes clear that the fear (al-wajal, "fear, trepidation") mentioned here is khawf (fear, dread). This is because of what is said about the same story in Hud: ﴿And he sensed fear of them. They said, "Do not fear."﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 70], and what is said in al-Dhariyat: ﴿So he sensed fear of them. They said, "Do not fear."﴾ [Hud: 28]. We have already noted that among the kinds of clarification (bayan) in this book is clarifying a word by a synonym that is more well known than it, as here, because khawf (fear) is a synonym (muradif) of wajal and is more well known. It also makes clear that the cause of his fear was that they did not eat, as in his saying: ﴿But when he saw their hands not reaching toward it, he disliked them and sensed fear of them﴾ [Hud: 70].

The Quranic verse: ﴿They said, "Do not fear. We give you good news of a boy endowed with knowledge."﴾

In this noble verse, God mentions that those noble guests, who are angels, gave Ibrahim (Abraham) the good news of a boy described as possessing knowledge ('ilm). A parallel to this is His statement, also in al-Dhariyat: ﴿They said, "Do not fear." And they gave him good news of a boy endowed with knowledge.﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 28] God has made clear that this boy is Ishaq (Isaac), as His statement in al-Dhariyat clarifies: ﴿And they gave him good news of a boy endowed with knowledge. Then his wife came forward in a loud cry and struck her face and said, "An old, barren woman!" They said, "So will it be; your Lord has said, indeed He is the Wise, the Knowing."﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 28–30]. Her coming forward "in a ṣarra," that is, with a shriek and an outcry, and her striking her face, meaning slapping it while saying she is an old, barren woman, indicates that the boy mentioned is her son, as is clear. It is further clarified by God's explicit statement of the good news given to her, that she would bear him, naming him and his son Ya'qub (Jacob). This is in His statement concerning the same story in Hud: ﴿And his wife was standing, and she laughed, so We gave her good news of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub.﴾ ﴿She said, "Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and this is my husband, an old man? Indeed, this is an astonishing thing!"﴾ [Hud: 71–72]

As for the boy who was given good news to Ibrahim, described as forbearing (ḥilm), mentioned in al-Saffat in His statement: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."﴾ ﴿"My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous."﴾ ﴿So We gave him good news of a forbearing boy.﴾ ﴿And when he reached with him the age of exertion, he said, "O my son, indeed I see in a dream that I am slaughtering you..."﴾ [al-Saffat: 99–102] — he is Isma'il (Ishmael). You will see, God willing (p-٢٨١) in the commentary on Surat al-Saffat, the evidence of the Quranic verses that the one to be sacrificed is Isma'il and not Ishaq, in a decisive manner that settles the dispute.

The word ghulam (boy, young man) is used in the language of the Arabs for a slave, for a young child who has not reached maturity, and for an adult man. Among its use for an adult is the verse of 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, on the day of al-Nahrawan:

"I am the young man of Quraysh, the trusted one,
Abu Husayn, so know this, and al-Hasan."

And the saying of Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal al-Sulami to Hassan, may God be pleased with them both:

"Meet the edge of the sword on my behalf, for I
am a young man; when I am provoked, I am no poet."

And the saying of Layla al-Akhyaliyya, praising al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf:

"When al-Hajjaj descends upon a sick land,
he pursues its deepest ailment and cures it.

He cures it of the stubborn disease that is in it,
a young man who, when he shakes the spear, gives it drink."

It is sometimes said of a female, ghulama (a girl), and from it is the saying of Aws ibn Ghalfa' al-Hujaymi describing a mare:

"And a galloping mare, of purebred stock, whose sire
—to her the ghulama and the ghulam are shown deference."

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 54:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "Do you give me good news although old age has touched me?"﴾.

In this noble verse, God, may He be exalted, makes clear that His prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) said that at the time of the good news of Ishaq (Isaac), old age had touched him. In Hud, He also stated that his wife said that he was an old man, in His saying about her: ﴿and this, my husband, is an old man﴾ [Hud: 72]. Likewise, she herself stated that at the time of the good news she was an elderly woman of advanced age, as in His saying in Hud: ﴿"Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman?"﴾ [Hud: 72], and His saying in al-Dhariyat: ﴿So she struck her face and said, "An old barren woman!"﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 29]. In another place, He made clear, concerning His prophet Ibrahim, that at the time God granted him his son Isma'il, he was also of advanced age. This is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Praise be to God who has granted me, in old age, Isma'il and Ishaq. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴾ [Ibrahim: 39].

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So for what do you give good news?﴾.

The apparent meaning is that the prophet of God, Ibrahim, peace be upon him and our Prophet, asked the angels with his saying ﴿So for what do you give good news?﴾ [al-Hijr: 54] as an interrogative of wonder at the perfection of God's power, may He be exalted. This is supported by the fact that He, may He be exalted, mentioned that what happened to him happened similarly to his wife, when she said ﴿Shall I give birth while I am an old woman?﴾. God, may He be exalted, has also made clear that this question of hers was out of wonder at that matter which breaks the normal custom, in His saying: ﴿They said, "Do you wonder at the command of God?"﴾ [Hud: 73], and the occurrence of a similar thing is also evidence for it from the prophet of God, Zakariyya (Zechariah), peace be upon him and our Prophet, since when he said: ﴿My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring﴾ [Al 'Imran: 38].

(p-282) And His saying: ﴿So the angels called him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary, "Indeed, God gives you good news of Yahya (John)"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 39]. He wondered at the perfection of God's power and said: ﴿"My Lord, how will I have a boy when old age has already reached me and my wife is barren?"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 40]. As for His saying ﴿So for what do you give good news?﴾, Ibn 'Amir, Abu 'Amr, 'Asim, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read it with a fatha on the nun, lightened (mukhaffafa), and it is the nun of raf' (the nun marking the indicative present verb, nun al-raf'). Nafi' read it with a kasra on the nun, lightened, and it is the nun of wiqaya (the nun protecting the verb's final vowel from clashing with the pronoun suffix, nun al-wiqaya), with the deletion of the ya' of the speaker (the first-person pronoun ya') because the kasra indicates it. Ibn Kathir read it with a kasra on the nun, doubled (mushaddada), with a long vowel. According to the reading of Ibn Kathir, he did not delete the nun of raf' nor the object; rather, the nun of raf' is assimilated into the nun of wiqaya, and the ya' of the speaker is the object. According to the reading of the majority, the nun of raf' is present and the object is elided, in accordance with the saying of Ibn Malik:

*"Deletion of a non-essential element is permitted if it does not harm, like the deletion of what was cited as an answer or restricted."*

According to the reading of Nafi', the nun of raf' is elided because it is burdensome for it to occur together with the nun of wiqaya.

**Note**

The deletion of the nun of raf' has five cases. Three of them make its deletion obligatory, one permits both deletion and retention, and one restricts its deletion to what is heard (from the Arabs). As for the three in which deletion is obligatory: the first is when a jussive operator (' amil jazm) enters upon the verb; the second is when an accusative operator (' amil nasb) enters upon it; and the third is when the verb is emphasized with the heavy emphatic nun (nun al-tawkid al-thaqila), as in *latublawunna* (you will surely be tested). As for the case in which both retention and deletion are permitted, it is when the nun of raf' occurs together with the nun of wiqaya, because the object is the ya' of the speaker; so both deletion and retention are permitted. From the deletion is the reading of Nafi' in this verse, *fa-bima tubashshirunni* with a kasra, and likewise His saying: ﴿He said, "Do you argue with me about God?"﴾ [al-An'am: 80]. And His saying: ﴿And He will say, "Where are My partners whom you used to oppose?"﴾ [al-Nahl: 27], with a kasra on the nun and lightening in the plural as well; and His saying: ﴿Say, "Is it other than God that you order me to worship?"﴾ [al-Zumar: 64], with a kasra and also lightening. All of these were read by some reciters with doubling, to retain the nun of raf' and assimilate it into the nun of wiqaya. As for the fifth case, restricted to what is heard, it is the deletion of the nun for a reason other than the four mentioned reasons, like the saying of the rajaz poet:

*"I spend the night telling stories while you spend the night rubbing / your face with ambergris and fragrant musk."*

As for the retention of the nun of raf' with a jussive particle, in His saying:

*"Were it not for the horsemen of Nu'm and their family / on the day of al-Sulayfa, they would not keep their word to the neighbour."*

This is rare, since *lam* is treated as analogous to its sister particles, not to the negating *la* or *ma*. It has also been said that it is a dialect of a people, as stated in al-Tashil. Likewise the retention of the nun with the accusative particle in His saying:

*"That you two read to Asma', woe to you both, / my greetings, and that you do not make anyone aware."*

This is a dialect of a people who treated the verbal *an* as analogous to its sister, the verbal *ma*, in not making the verb accusative with it, as indicated in al-Khulasa by his saying:

*"Some have left *an* inactive, by analogy / with its sister *ma*, though it deserves to govern."*

The fact that Ibrahim's question was an interrogative of wonder at the perfection of God's power does not conflict with the angels' words to him, as God reported about them: ﴿They said, "We have given you good news in truth, so do not be of those who despair."﴾ [al-Hijr: 55], on the evidence of His saying: ﴿He said, "And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except the astray?"﴾ [al-Hijr: 56]. This is because it is evidence that his interrogative was not an interrogative of denial nor of despair. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 56:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except those who are astray?"﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, makes clear that His Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) said to the angels that none despairs of the mercy of Allah, exalted is He, except those who have strayed from the path of truth. He also makes clear that this same meaning was stated by Ya'qub (Jacob), son of Ishaq (Isaac), son of Ibrahim, to his sons in His saying: ﴿O my sons, go and search for news of Yusuf and his brother, and do not despair of the comfort (rawh) of Allah. Indeed, none despairs of the comfort of Allah except the disbelieving people.﴾ [Yusuf: 87]. Abu Hayyan said in al-Bahr al-Muhit (The Surrounding Sea), in his tafsir of His saying: ﴿Indeed, none despairs of the comfort of Allah﴾, the verse: "The rawh (comfort) of Allah is His mercy, His relief, and His easing."

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿قالُوا إنّا أُرْسِلْنا إلى قَوْمٍ مُجْرِمِينَ﴾ ﴿إلّا آلَ لُوطٍ﴾ .

أشارَ في هَذِهِ الآيَةِ الكَرِيمَةِ إلى أنَّ المُرادَ بِهَؤُلاءِ القَوْمِ المُجْرِمِينَ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ الَّذِينَ أُرْسِلَ إلَيْهِمْ فَكَذَّبُوهُ، ووَجْهُ إشارَتِهِ تَعالى لِذَلِكَ اسْتِثْناءُ لُوطٍ وأهْلِهِ غَيْرَ امْرَأتِهِ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إلّا آلَ لُوطٍ إنّا لَمُنَجُّوهم أجْمَعِينَ إلا امْرَأتَهُ﴾ الآيَةَ [الحجر: ٥٩ - ٦٠] وصَرَّحَ بِأنَّهم قَوْمُ لُوطٍ

• بِقَوْلِهِ في هُودٍ في القِصَّةِ بِعَيْنِها: ﴿قالُوا لا تَخَفْ إنّا أُرْسِلْنا إلى قَوْمِ لُوطٍ﴾ الآيَةَ [هود: ٧٠] وصَرَّحَ في الذّارِياتِ بِأنَّهم أُرْسِلُوا إلى هَؤُلاءِ القَوْمِ المُجْرِمِينَ لِيُرْسِلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ حِجارَةً مِن طِينٍ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿قالُوا إنّا أُرْسِلْنا إلى قَوْمٍ مُجْرِمِينَ﴾ ﴿لِنُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهِمْ حِجارَةً مِن طِينٍ﴾ [الذاريات: ٣٢ - ٣٣] وصَرَّحَ في العَنْكَبُوتِ أنَّهم قالُوا إنَّهم مُهْلِكُوهم بِسَبَبِ ظُلْمِهِمْ، ومُنْزِلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ (p-284) رِجْزًا مِنَ السَّماءِ بِسَبَبِ فِسْقِهِمْ وذَلِكَ في قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَلَمّا جاءَتْ رُسُلُنا إبْراهِيمَ بِالبُشْرى قالُوا إنّا مُهْلِكُو أهْلِ هَذِهِ القَرْيَةِ إنَّ أهْلَها كانُوا ظالِمِينَ﴾ ﴿قالَ إنَّ فِيها لُوطًا قالُوا نَحْنُ أعْلَمُ بِمَن فِيها﴾ الآيَةَ [العنكبوت: ٣١ - ٣٢]،

• وقَوْلِهِ: ﴿وَقالُوا لا تَخَفْ ولا تَحْزَنْ إنّا مُنَجُّوكَ وأهْلَكَ إلّا امْرَأتَكَ كانَتْ مِنَ الغابِرِينَ﴾ ﴿إنّا مُنْزِلُونَ عَلى أهْلِ هَذِهِ القَرْيَةِ رِجْزًا مِنَ السَّماءِ بِما كانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ﴾ [العنكبوت: ٣٣ - ٣٤]

• وقَوْلِهِ: ﴿إلّا آلَ لُوطٍ إنّا لَمُنَجُّوهم أجْمَعِينَ﴾ [الحجر: ٥٩] بَيَّنَ في هَذِهِ الآيَةِ الكَرِيمَةِ أنَّهُ اسْتَثْنى آلَ لُوطٍ مِن ذَلِكَ العَذابِ النّازِلِ بِقَوْمِهِ، وأوْضَحَ هَذا المَعْنى في آياتٍ أُخَرَ كَما تَقَدَّمَ في هُودٍ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿قالُوا يالُوطُ إنّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَنْ يَصِلُوا إلَيْكَ فَأسْرِ بِأهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ ولا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكم أحَدٌ إلّا امْرَأتَكَ﴾ الآيَةَ [هود: ٨١]

• وقَوْلِهِ في العَنْكَبُوتِ: ﴿وَقالُوا لا تَخَفْ ولا تَحْزَنْ إنّا مُنَجُّوكَ وأهْلَكَ إلّا امْرَأتَكَ﴾ الآيَةَ [العنكبوت: ٣٣]

• وقَوْلِهِ ﴿فَأنْجَيْناهُ وأهْلَهُ إلّا امْرَأتَهُ كانَتْ مِنَ الغابِرِينَ﴾ [الأعراف: ٨٣]

• وقَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَنَجَّيْناهُ وأهْلَهُ أجْمَعِينَ﴾ ﴿إلّا عَجُوزًا في الغابِرِينَ﴾ الآيَةَ [الشعراء: ١٧٠ - ١٧١]

• وقَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَأنْجَيْناهُ وأهْلَهُ إلّا امْرَأتَهُ قَدَّرْناها مِنَ الغابِرِينَ﴾ [النمل: ٥٧]

إلى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الآياتِ.

وَما ذَكَرَ في هَذِهِ الآيَةِ الكَرِيمَةِ مِنِ اسْتِثْناءِ امْرَأتِهِ مِن أهْلِهِ النّاجِينَ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إلّا امْرَأتَهُ قَدَّرْنا إنَّها لَمِنَ الغابِرِينَ﴾ أوْضَحَهُ في هَذِهِ الآياتِ الَّتِي ذَكَرْنا آنِفًا ونَحْوَها مِنَ الآياتِ، وبَيَّنَ في الذّارِياتِ أنَّهُ أنْجى مَن كانَ في قَوْمِ لُوطٍ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ، وأنَّهم لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهِمْ مِنَ المُسْلِمِينَ إلّا بَيْتٌ واحِدٌ وهم آلُ لُوطٍ وذَلِكَ في قَوْلِهِ ﴿فَأخْرَجْنا مَن كانَ فِيها مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ ﴿فَما وجَدْنا فِيها غَيْرَ بَيْتٍ مِنَ المُسْلِمِينَ﴾ [العنكبوت: ٣٥ - ٣٦] .

تَنْبِيهٌ

فِي هَذِهِ الآيَةِ الكَرِيمَةِ دَلِيلٌ واضِحٌ لِما حَقَّقَهُ عُلَماءُ الأُصُولِ (the scholars of the principles of jurisprudence, uṣūl al-fiqh) مِن جَوازِ الِاسْتِثْناءِ مِنَ الِاسْتِثْناءِ (istithnāʾ min al-istithnāʾ, an exception from an exception)؛ لِأنَّهُ تَعالى اسْتَثْنى آلَ لُوطٍ مِن إهْلاكِ المُجْرِمِينَ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿إلّا آلَ لُوطٍ إنّا لَمُنَجُّوهم أجْمَعِينَ﴾ [الحجر: ٥٩] ثُمَّ اسْتَثْنى مِن هَذا الِاسْتِثْناءِ امْرَأةَ لُوطٍ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿إلّا امْرَأتَهُ قَدَّرْنا إنَّها لَمِنَ الغابِرِينَ﴾ [الحجر: ٦٠] وبِهَذا تَعْلَمُ أنَّ قَوْلَ ابْنِ مالِكٍ (Ibn Malik) في الخُلاصَةِ (al-Khulasah):

؎وَحُكْمُها في القَصْدِ حُكْمُ الأوَّلِ

لَيْسَ صَحِيحًا عَلى إطْلاقِهِ. وأوْضَحَ مَسْألَةَ تَعَدُّدِ الِاسْتِثْناءِ بِأقْسامِها صاحِبُ مَراقِي (p-285) السُّعُودِ (Marāqī al-Suʿūd) في مَبْحَثِ المُخَصَّصِ المُتَّصِلِ (al-mukhaṣṣiṣ al-muttaṣil, the connected specifier) بِقَوْلِهِ:

؎وَذا تَعَدُّدٍ بِعَطْفٍ حَصَلَ ∗∗∗ بِالِاتِّفاقِ مُسْجَلًا لِلْأوَّلْ

؎إلّا فَكُلٌّ لِلَّذِي بِهِ اتَّصَلْ ∗∗∗ وكُلُّها مَعَ التَّساوِي قَدْ بَطَلْ

؎إنْ كانَ غَيْرُ الأوَّلِ المُسْتَغْرَقا ∗∗∗ فالكُلُّ لِلْمُخْرَجِ مِنهُ حُقِّقا

؎وَحَيْثُما اسْتَغْرَقَ الاوَّلَ فَقَطْ ∗∗∗ فَألْغِ واعْتَبِرْ بِخُلْفٍ في النَّمَطْ

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So when the messengers came to the family of Lut﴾ ﴿he said, "Indeed, you are a people unknown to me."﴾

In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted explains that when the angels, the messengers sent to destroy his people, came to Lut, peace be upon him and upon our Prophet, he said to them: ﴿Indeed, you are a people unknown to me.﴾ In other places He states that his coming upon them caused him distress and that he was greatly troubled by it:

• As in His saying in Hud: ﴿And when Our messengers came to Lut, he was distressed for them and felt helpless regarding them, and he said, "This is a trying day."﴾ [Hud: 77]

• And His saying in al-Ankabut: ﴿And when Our messengers came to Lut, he was distressed for them and felt helpless regarding them﴾ [al-Ankabut: 33]. In al-Dhariyat, He mentions that His prophet Ibrahim also said to them, "A people unknown," just as He mentioned of Lut here, in His saying: ﴿He said, "Peace." "A people unknown."﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 25]

• As for His saying ﴿a people unknown﴾, it has been said that its meaning is that they were not known to him. The word nakira is the opposite of ma'rifa (recognized). It has also been said that he saw them in the form of young men of handsome faces, and he feared that his people would commit upon them the abomination of sodomy (liwat), so he said: ﴿Indeed, you are a people unknown to me﴾ [al-Hijr: 62]. Al-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf: "Munkarun means that my self rejects you and recoils from you, so I fear that you will come upon me with evil," as evidenced by His saying: ﴿Rather, we have brought you that about which they used to doubt﴾ ﴿and We have brought you the truth﴾, and the verse [al-Hijr: 63-64]. This interpretation is supported by the fact that in Hud He made clear that the cause of Ibrahim's rejection of them was that they did not eat of the calf he had offered them, as in His saying: ﴿But when he saw that their hands did not reach toward it, he regarded them with suspicion and felt a fear of them﴾ [Hud: 70], because whoever is hosted and refrains from eating is feared to bring harm.

• As for His saying in these verses: ﴿Indeed, We will save them﴾ [al-Hijr: 59], Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited it with a sukun on the nun after the damma on the mim, with the lightened form, as the active participle of anja on the pattern af'ala. Others among the reciters recited it with a fatha on the nun and a shadda on the jim, as the passive participle of nujjiya on the pattern fu'\u0031\u0061 with gemination. The meanings of al-inja' (إنجاء) and al-tanjiya (تنجية) are the same.

• As for His saying: ﴿We have decreed that she is of those who remain behind﴾ [al-Hijr: 60], Abu Bakr, from Asim, recited it with a lightened dal, and others recited it with a doubled dal. Both are dialectal forms with the same meaning.

• As for His saying: ﴿came to the family of Lut﴾ [al-Hijr: 61], Qalun, al-Bazzi, and Abu 'Amr recited it by dropping the first hamza and making the second hamza clear, with both qasr and madd. Warsh recited it by making the first hamza clear and replacing the second hamza with an alif, with both qasr and madd. From Warsh there is also making the first hamza clear and softening the second hamza, with qasr, tawassut, and madd. Qunbul recited it like Warsh's reading, except that with softening he has only qasr. The rest recited it by making both hamzas clear, and each follows his own principle regarding madd. What has been mentioned of the recitations of Warsh and Qunbul is the making-clear reading transmitted from them, even though others have been mentioned, and Allah knows best.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And the people of the city came, rejoicing.﴾

The reason for the joy of Lot's people was that they thought the angels were young men from among the sons of Adam, and their souls prompted them to commit against them the vile act of sodomy (liwat). This is indicated by the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, these are my guests, so do not disgrace me﴾ [al-Hijr: 68], and His words: ﴿And they had already sought to seduce him from his guests, so We obliterated their eyes﴾ [al-Qamar: 37], and His words: ﴿And his people came rushing toward him, and before that they had been doing evil deeds﴾ [Hud: 78], and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 75:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for those who observe with insight.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, may He be exalted, shows that in what He inflicted of punishment upon the people of Lut there are signs for those who reflect upon it, through which they attain admonition, consideration, and fear of disobeying Allah, lest He bring upon them the like of that punishment which He sent down upon the people of Lut when they disobeyed Him and denied His messenger. This meaning is made clear in other places:

• As in His saying in al-'Ankabut: ﴿And We have left from it a clear sign for a people who reason﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 35].

• And His saying in adh-Dhariyat: ﴿And We left in it a sign for those who fear the painful punishment﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 37].

• And His saying here: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for those who observe with insight﴾ [al-Hijr: 75].

• And His saying in ash-Shu'ara', after mentioning the story of the people of Lut: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 174], and the rest of the verse.

Just as He stated the same in the destruction of the people of Nuh, the people of Hud, the people of Salih, and the people of Shu'ayb in ash-Shu'ara'.

His saying ﴿lil-mutawassimin﴾ (for those who observe with insight): the root of at-tawassum is tafa''ul from al-wasm, which is the mark by which something else is inferred. It is said: "tawassamtu fihi al-khayr" (I perceived goodness in him) when I saw its mark (mismam) in him, i.e., its sign that indicates it. From this is the saying of 'Abdullah ibn Rawahah, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the Prophet ﷺ:

*I have perceived in you goodness, which I recognize, and Allah knows that my gaze is steadfast.*

And another said:

*I perceived him when I saw a majesty upon him, and I said: he is a man of the family of Hashim.*

This is the origin of at-tawassum. The scholars have statements on it that are close in meaning, all of which return to one thing. From Qatadah: ﴿lil-mutawassimin﴾ means "lil-mu'tabirin" (those who take admonition). From Mujahid: it means "al-mutafarrisin" (those who discern by insight). From Ibn 'Abbas and ad-Dahhak: it means "lil-nazirin" (those who look). From Malik, from some people of Madinah: it means "lil-mutaammilin" (those who reflect).

It is not hidden that consideration, looking, discerning, and reflecting have one meaning. Likewise the statement of Ibn Zayd and Muqatil: it means "lil-mutafakkirin" (those who ponder), and the statement of Abu 'Ubaydah: it means "lil-mutabassirin" (those who see clearly). So the sum of all these statements returns to one thing: that what befell the people of Lut contains admonition and lesson for whoever looks at it and reflects upon it with true reflection. The application of at-tawassum to reflection, looking, and consideration is well known in the speech of the Arabs. From it is the saying of Zuhayr:

*And in them is delight for the friend, and a sight graceful to the eye of the one who looks and observes.*

That is, the one who reflects upon that beauty. And the saying of Tarif ibn Tamim al-'Anbari:

*Or whenever a tribe came to 'Ukaz, they sent to me their spokesman, observing and reflecting.*

That is, he looks and reflects.

The author of ad-Durr al-Manthur said: Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿la-ayatin lil-mutawassimin﴾ [al-Hijr: 75], that he said: "lil-nazirin" (for those who look).

'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azamah related from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿la-ayatin lil-mutawassimin﴾, that he said: "lil-mu'tabirin" (for those who take admonition). Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿la-ayatin lil-mutawassimin﴾, that he said: "they are al-mutafarrisun" (those who discern by insight). Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah related from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, concerning His saying: Indeed, in that ﴿la-ayatin lil-mutawassimin﴾, that he said: "they are al-mutafarrisun." Al-Bukhari in his Tarikh, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Sunni, and Abu Nu'aym together in at-Tibb, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Khatib related from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Beware the firasah (insight) of the believer, for he looks with the light of Allah,'" then he recited ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for those who observe with insight﴾ and said: "lil-mutafarrisin" (for those who discern by insight). Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Beware the firasah of the believer, for the believer looks with the light of Allah." Ibn Jarir related from Thawban, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Beware the firasah of the believer, for he looks with the light of Allah and speaks with the success of Allah." Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, al-Bazzar, Ibn al-Sunni, and Abu Nu'aym related from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, Allah has servants who recognize people through tawassum." End.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 76:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, it is on a road that remains.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted explains that the dwellings of the people of Lot, and the traces of Allah's destruction of them, lie on a road that remains, i.e., a established path that people travel, not yet effaced. The people of the Hijaz pass by them on their journeys to the Levant (al-Sham). The meaning is that the traces of Allah's destruction of them, which you witness on your travels, contain for you a lesson and a deterrent, obliging you to beware of doing as they did, lest Allah bring down upon you the like of what He brought down upon them. He clarified this meaning in other places,

such as His saying: ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning, and at night. Will you not then reason?﴾ [As-Saffat: 137-138];

and His saying, concerning them and the dwellers of the Thicket: ﴿Have they not traveled through the land and seen what was the end of those before them? Allah destroyed them, and for the disbelievers are the like thereof.﴾ [Muhammad: 10]

and His saying concerning them and the dwellers of the Thicket: ﴿And indeed, both were on a clear highway.﴾ [Al-Hijr: 79],

and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 78:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, the companions of the Thicket were wrongdoers﴾ ﴿So We took retribution from them﴾.

In this verse, He - may He be glorified and exalted - mentions that the companions of the Thicket (al-Ayka) were wrongdoers, and that He, may He be glorified and exalted, took retribution from them because of their wrongdoing. He explained this story in other places, such as His saying in ash-Shu'ara': ﴿The companions of the Thicket denied the messengers﴾ ﴿When Shu'ayb said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"﴾ ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger﴾ ﴿So fear Allah and obey me﴾ ﴿And I do not ask you for it any payment; my payment is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ ﴿Give full measure and do not be among the deprivers﴾ ﴿And weigh with an even balance﴾ ﴿And do not deprive people of their things and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing corruption﴾ ﴿And fear Him who created you and the former generations﴾ ﴿They said, "You are only of those affected by magic"﴾ ﴿And you are not but a human like us, and indeed we think you are among the liars﴾ ﴿So cause a piece of the sky to fall upon us, if you should be of the truthful"﴾ ﴿He said, "My Lord is most knowing of what you do"﴾ ﴿So they denied him, and the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day﴾ ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 176-190]. So in this verse He clarified that their wrongdoing was their denial of their messenger and their cheating in measure, and their depriving people of their things, and that His retribution against them was the punishment of the Day of the Shade. He also clarified that it was the punishment of a tremendous day. The "Shade" (ath-Thulla) is a cloud that overshadowed them, then Allah set it ablaze with fire upon them, and it burned them. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted.

Nafi', Ibn 'Amir and Ibn Kathir read "Layka" in ash-Shu'ara' and Sad, with an open lam at the beginning of the word, an open ta' at its end, without a hamza and without the definite article, on the basis that it is a proper noun for the town, not inflected (ghayr munsarif). Abu 'Amr, 'Asim, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "al-Ayka" with the definite article, the hamza, and a kasra on the ta'. All the readers read it this way in Qaf and al-Hijr. Abu 'Ubayda said: Layka and al-Ayka are the name of their city, like Makka and Bakka. In the language of the Arabs, al-Ayka means a thicket (ghaydha), which is a group of trees, and the plural is al-Ayk. They were called "companions of the Thicket" because they were companions of thickets (ghiyad) (p-289) and meadows (riyad). It is related that their trees were doum palms, which is the muqil. From the use of al-Ayka for a thicket is the saying of an-Nabigha:

"It polishes, with the two feathers of a dove of a thicket, cold hail whose gums are tinged with antimony."

Al-Jawhari said in his Sihah: Whoever reads "Ashab al-Ayka" means the thicket, and whoever reads "Layka" means the name of the town, and it is said: they are like Bakka and Makka. Some scholars said: al-Ayka is a tree, and al-Ayk is the intertwined trees.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 80 (part 1 of 5):

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the companions of al-Hijr denied the messengers.﴾

Al-Hijr (the dwellings of Thamud between the Hijaz and the Levant, near Wadi al-Qura). The meaning of the noble verse is: ﴿Thamud denied the messengers.﴾ The Exalted has made clear Thamud's denial of their prophet Salih, peace be upon him and upon our Prophet, in other places:

• As in His saying: ﴿Thamud denied the messengers when their brother Salih said to them, "Will you not fear God?"﴾ and so on [al-Shu'ara': 141].
• And His saying: ﴿So they denied him and hamstrung her [the she-camel]﴾ [al-Shams: 14].
• And His saying: ﴿Thamud denied the warnings. And they said, "Shall we follow a single human being from among us? Indeed, we would then be in error and madness."﴾ [al-Qamar: 23–24].
• And His saying: ﴿So they hamstrung the she-camel and defied the command of their Lord, and said, "O Salih, bring us what you promise us, if you are indeed among the messengers."﴾ [al-A'raf: 77].
along with other verses.

He said that they denied the messengers, although the one they denied was Salih alone, because the call of all the messengers is one, and it is the realization of the meaning of "There is no god but God," as the Exalted has clarified with general and specific proofs. Generalizing for all of them, He said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no god but I, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25]. He said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship God and avoid the Taghut"﴾ [al-Nahl: 36]. He said: ﴿And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods other than the Most Merciful to be worshipped?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 45], along with other verses.

And in specifying the messengers by their names, He said: ﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he said, "O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 23]. He said: ﴿And to 'Ad [We sent] their brother Hud. He said, "O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him"﴾ [Hud: 50]. He said: ﴿And to Midian [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him"﴾ [Hud: 84], along with other verses.

So when you realize that the call of the messengers is one, you know that whoever denies one of them has denied them all. For this reason the Exalted declared that whoever disbelieves in some of them is truly a disbeliever. He said: ﴿And they say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and they intend to adopt a way between that. Those are the disbelievers in truth﴾ [al-Nisa': 150–151]. (p-390) He also made clear that no distinction may be made among them, in His saying: ﴿We make no distinction between any of them﴾ [2:136 and 3:84], and His saying: ﴿We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285]. He promised reward for not distinguishing among them, in His saying: ﴿And those who believe in God and His messengers and do not distinguish between any of them — those, He will give them their rewards﴾ [al-Nisa': 152]. We have treated this matter in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab."

Note.

Know that he, ﷺ, passed by the al-Hijr mentioned in this verse on his way during the expedition of Tabuk. Al-Bukhari related in his Sahih, in the chapter on the expedition of Tabuk, from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "When the Prophet ﷺ passed by al-Hijr, he said: 'Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, lest what befell them befall you, unless you are weeping.' Then he covered his head and hastened his pace until he crossed the valley." This is the wording of al-Bukhari. Al-Bukhari also related in the Book of the Stories of the Prophets, from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ alighted at al-Hijr during the expedition of Tabuk, he commanded them not to drink from its well or draw water from it. They said: 'We have kneaded dough with it and drawn water.' So he commanded them to throw away that dough and spill that water." Then al-Bukhari said: And it is narrated from Sabrah ibn Ma'bad and Abu al-Shamus that the Prophet ﷺ commanded the food to be thrown away. Then he said: And Abu Dharr said, from the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever kneads with its water..."

Then he related with his chain, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he informed him: "The people alighted with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the land of Thamud, al-Hijr, and drew water from its well and kneaded with it. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded them to spill what they had drawn from their wells, and to feed the dough to the camels, and he commanded them to draw water from the well which the she-camel used to drink from."

Then he said: Usamah related it similarly from Nafi'. Then he related with his chain, from Salim ibn 'Abdullah, from his father: "When the Prophet ﷺ passed by al-Hijr, he said: 'Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, unless you are weeping, lest what befell them befall you.' Then he covered himself with his garment while on his mount."

Then he also related with his chain, from Salim, that Ibn 'Umar said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, unless you are weeping, lest what befell them befall you.'" All of this is the wording of al-Bukhari in his Sahih.

Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath: As for the hadith of Sabrah ibn Ma'bad, it was connected by Ahmad (p-291) and al-Tabarani through the chain of 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn al-Rabi' ibn Sabrah ibn Ma'bad, from his father, from his grandfather Sabrah — with an unpointed sin, a sukun on the unpointed... [the vowelling as in the source] — al-Juhani, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his companions when he departed from al-Hijr: 'Whoever among you has kneaded a dough with this water, or cooked a stew, let him throw it away.'" Sabrah ibn Ma'bad has no narration in al-Bukhari other than this place. As for the hadith of Abu al-Shamus — with a dotted letter then an unpointed one — and he is a Bakri whose name is not known, al-Bukhari connected it in al-Adab al-Mufrad, and al-Tabarani and Ibn Mandah through the chain of Sulaym ibn Mutayr, from his father, from him, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ... " and he mentioned the hadith, in which: "The one who had kneaded threw away his dough, and the one who had cooked threw away his stew." Ibn Abi 'Asim related it through this route and added: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have cooked a stew, shall I give it to my mount?' He said: 'Yes.'"

Ibn Hajar also said: His saying, "Abu Dharr said, from the Prophet ﷺ: 'Whoever kneads with its water,'" was connected by al-Bazzar through the chain of 'Abd Allah ibn Qudamah from him: "They were with the Prophet ﷺ in the expedition of Tabuk, and they came upon a valley. The Prophet ﷺ said to them: 'You are in a cursed valley, so hasten.' And he said: 'Whoever has kneaded a dough, or cooked a pot, let him overturn it.'" The hadith... He said: I do not know it except through this chain. Al-Bukhari related in the commentary on the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And the companions of al-Hijr denied the messengers﴾ [al-Hijr: 80], from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the companions of al-Hijr: 'Do not enter upon these people unless you are weeping; if you are not weeping, do not enter upon them, lest there befall you the like of what befell them.'" Al-Bukhari also related, from Ibn 'Umar, in the Book of Prayer, in the chapter on prayer in places of subsidence and punishment: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Do not enter upon these punished people unless you are weeping; if you are not weeping, do not enter upon them, lest there befall you what befell them.'" Some of these narrations that we have mentioned from al-Bukhari were also related by Muslim in his Sahih. Both of them agree on the prohibition of entering their dwellings except in a state of weeping, and on his ﷺ hastening until he passed their dwellings. In these authentic narrations there is the prohibition of entering the places of subsidence and punishment except in a state of weeping, and in them is the hastening to pass them, and not drawing water from their waters, and not eating food kneaded with them. From here some scholars said: it is not permissible to perform purification with their water, and prayer in them is not valid, because since their water is unfit for eating and drinking, it is known that it is unfit for purification, which is an act of drawing near to Allah, the Exalted.

Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih: Chapter: Prayer in places of subsidence and punishment: "And it is mentioned that 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, disliked praying at the subsidence of Babel." Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath: This report was related by Ibn Abi Shaybah through the chain of 'Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Muhill — with a dammah on the meem, a kasrah on the unpointed letter, and a shaddah on the lam — who said: "We were with 'Ali, and we passed by the subsidence at Babel, and he did not pray until he had passed it — i.e., went beyond it." And through another route, from 'Ali, who said: "I would not pray in a land which Allah has caused to subside three times." The apparent meaning is that his saying "three times" is not connected to the subsidence, for there was only one subsidence there. Rather, he meant that 'Ali said that three times. Abu Dawud related it in a marfu' form through another route from 'Ali, with the wording: "My beloved ﷺ forbade me to pray in the land of Babel, for it is cursed," in whose chain there is weakness. The fitting interpretation of the author's citation is what has preceded. The subsidence meant here is what Allah the Exalted mentioned in His saying: ﴿So Allah came at their structure from its foundations, and the roof fell on them from above them﴾ [al-Nahl: 26]. The people of tafsir and reports mentioned that Nimrod ibn Canaan built there a great structure, said to have been five thousand cubits in height, and Allah caused them to subside. Al-Khattabi said: "I know of no scholar who forbade prayer in the land of Babel." End of quotation from Fath al-Bari, the point of relevance.

And al-Khattabi's statement is contradicted by what I have seen from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him; yet the general sense of the sound hadith supports it: "The earth has been made for us a place of prostration and a purifier," and the marfu' hadith of Abu Dawud from 'Ali, to which Ibn Hajar pointed, has weakness in its wording: "Ḥaddathana Sulayman ibn Dawud, akhbarana Ibn Wahb, qala haddathani Ibn Lahi'ah and Yahya ibn Azhar, from 'Ammar ibn Sa'd al-Muradi, from Abu Salih al-Ghifari: that 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by Babel while travelling, and the muezzin came to him announcing the 'Asr prayer. When he came out of it, he commanded the muezzin, and he gave the iqamah. When he finished, he said: 'My beloved ﷺ forbade me to pray in the graveyard, and forbade me to pray in the land of Babel, for it is cursed.'"

Ahmad ibn Salih related to us: Ibn Wahb related to us, Yahya ibn Azhar and Ibn Lahi'ah informed me, from al-Hajjaj ibn Shaddad, from Abu Salih al-Ghifari, from 'Ali, with the same meaning as Sulayman ibn Dawud, and he said: "When he went out — in place of 'when he came out' — " ended.

It may appear to the one who examines the two chains of this hadith that it is not below the rank of acceptability; but there is a hidden defect pointed out by Ibn Yunus. As for its not being below the rank of acceptability: its first route is at the head of its tiers: Sulayman ibn Dawud, and there is no disagreement that he is trustworthy (thiqah). In the second route: Ahmad ibn Salih in place of the aforementioned Sulayman, and Ahmad ibn Salih is trustworthy and a hafiz. The criticism of al-Nasa'i against him is an error that is rejected, as al-Iraqi said in his Alfiyyah:

"Often the criticism of the critic is rejected, like al-Nasa'i's concerning Ahmad ibn Salih."

The cause of his error in this was that Ibn Ma'in discredited Ahmad ibn Salih al-Shumuni. Al-Nasa'i thought that Ibn Ma'in's intention was this Ahmad ibn Salih, who is Abu Ja'far ibn al-Tabari al-Misri, but this is not so, as Ibn Hibban affirmed decisively.

The second tier in both chains:

Ibn Wahb, who is 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb ibn Muslim al-Qurashi, their client, Abu Muhammad al-Misri, trustworthy, a hafiz, an ascetic, well known.

The third tier of both chains: Yahya ibn Azhar and 'Abd Allah ibn Lahi'ah. Yahya ibn Azhar al-Basri, client of Quraysh, is truthful (saduq); 'Abd Allah ibn Lahi'ah is truthful, but became confused after his books were burned. The apparent view is that the strengthening of one of them by the other is not below the rank of good (hasan). This is supported by the fact that the transmitter of the hadith, Ibn Wahb, and it is well known that the narration of Ibn Wahb and Ibn al-Mubarak from Ibn Lahi'ah is more reliable than the narration of others from him.

The fourth tier in the first chain: 'Ammar ibn Sa'd al-Muradi. In the second chain: al-Hajjaj ibn Shaddad, and 'Ammar ibn Sa'd al-Muradi, then al-Salhami, and al-Hajjaj ibn Shaddad al-San'ani, resident of Egypt. Both are acceptable (maqbul), as Ibn Hajar said in al-Taqrib, and the strengthening of one by the other is not below the rank of good (hasan).

The fifth tier in both chains is Abu Salih al-Ghifari, whose name is Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Rahman. He is counted among the people of Egypt, and he is trustworthy (thiqah).

The sixth tier in both of them is Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him). So what appears is that the hadith is fit to be used as evidence, but it has a hidden defect (illah) which Ibn Yunus mentioned: the narration of Abu Salih al-Ghifari from 'Ali is mursal, as Ibn Hajar mentioned in al-Taqrib. Al-Bayhaqi said in al-Sunan al-Kubra: "Chapter: On those who disliked prayer in a place of earth-sinking and punishment." Abu 'Ali al-Rudhbari informed us, Abu Bakr ibn Dasah informed us, Abu Dawud related to us, and then he cited the hadith of Abu Dawud mentioned just above, with its wording in the text and both chains. Then he said: "And it has been related to us from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Muhill al-'Umari, who said: 'We were with 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and he passed by us at the sunken site which is at Babil, and he did not pray until he had passed it.'" And from Hujr al-Hadrami, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "I would not pray in a land in which Allah has sunk (the people) three times." Then al-Bayhaqi said: "This prohibition of prayer in it, if it is established as marfu', is not for a reason relating to the prayer itself; for if one prayed in it, he would not need to repeat it." Then al-Bayhaqi cited some of the narrations of the hadith of Ibn 'Umar which we mentioned earlier from al-Bukhari and Muslim. Then he said: "The Prophet ﷺ loved to leave those dwellings, and disliked to stay in them except weeping; so staying there for prayer and other things is included in that." End of quotation.

This is the summary of what has come concerning prayer in places of earth-sinking and performing ablution with their water. Some scholars held that prayer there is valid and ablution with its water is sufficient, and they relied on the general texts, such as his ﷺ saying: "The earth has been made for me entirely a place of prostration (masjid)," the hadith in full. And on the general evidences for lifting the minor ritual impurity (hadath) and removing the impurity (khabath) by pure water. Other scholars held that prayer there is not permissible and ablution with its water is not valid, and they relied on the marfu' hadith of 'Ali: that his beloved ﷺ forbade him from praying in the sunken site of Babil, because it is a cursed land. They said: "The prohibition requires invalidity, because what he ﷺ forbade is not of our affair, and 'whoever introduces into our affair what is not part of it, it is rejected' (radd), as is established in the hadith." They argued against the validity of ablution with its water by saying that the Prophet ﷺ forbade using it for eating and drinking, and these two are not acts of worship (qurbah); so this indicates the prohibition of purification with it a fortiori.

The one who has written this (may Allah pardon him) says: What appears to us to be the stronger view is that whoever passes by them should hasten in his walk until he exits them, as the Prophet ﷺ did, and as his in-law (sihr), his paternal cousin, and the father of his two grandsons did, may Allah be pleased with all of them; and that one should not enter them except weeping, due to the sound hadith. So if one descended there and prayed, the apparent ruling is that his prayer is valid, since no sound evidence has come with a clear indication of its invalidity; and ruling an act of worship invalid requires a text strong both in its wording and its indication. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.
