Note.
(p. 301) Know that what some who have no knowledge claim, namely that the Book and the Sunnah indicate the taking of graves as mosques, meaning by the Book His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those who prevailed in their affair said: "We will surely take over them a place of worship."﴾ [al-Kahf: 21], and meaning by the Sunnah what is established in the Sahih, that the site of the Prophet's ﷺ mosque had graves of the polytheists in it, is in the utmost weakness, and whoever says it is among the most ignorant of Allah's creation.

As for the answer to the argument from the verse, you say: Who are these people who said: ﴿We will surely take over them a place of worship﴾? Are they among those who are to be followed, or are they disbelievers whom it is not permitted to follow? Al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, said concerning these people [al-Kahf: 21], the following text: "It has been disputed who uttered this statement: were they the Muslim group, or the disbelievers? When you know that, know that if they are said to be disbelievers, there is no problem that their act is not evidence, since no one has held that the actions of disbelievers are evidence, as is necessarily known. And if they are said to be Muslims, as the mention of the mosque indicates, because taking mosques is one of the attributes of Muslims, then it is not hidden from the least intelligent person that the saying of a group of Muslims in past generations, 'They will do such and such,' does not oppose the clear sound texts from the Prophet ﷺ, except for one whom Allah has blinded in insight, who opposes their saying ﴿We will surely take over them a place of worship﴾ [al-Kahf: 21] with his ﷺ saying in his final illness, five days before he passed to the Highest Companion: 'May Allah curse the Jews and the Christians; they took the graves of their prophets as mosques.' The hadith... It becomes clear to you that whoever follows these people in taking a mosque over graves is cursed on the tongue of the Truthful, the one whose word is believed ﷺ, as is evident. And whoever is cursed on his ﷺ tongue is cursed in the Book of Allah, as was soundly reported from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him; because Allah says: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it﴾ [al-Hashr: 7]. For this reason Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, declared that the woman who connects hair, the woman who tattoos, and those mentioned with them in the hadith, each of them is cursed in the Book of Allah. He said to the woman who said to him: 'I read what is between the two covers and did not find it. If you had read it, you would have found it,' and then he recited the noble verse. His hadith is well known in the two Sahihs and others. By this you know that whoever takes mosques over graves is cursed in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, on the tongue of His Messenger ﷺ, and that there is no evidence in the verse ﴿We will surely take over them a place of worship﴾ [al-Kahf: 21]."

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 80 (part 4 of 5):**

As for the argument that the Mosque of the Prophet ﷺ in Medina was built on the site of the graves of the polytheists, its invalidity is evident, because the Prophet ﷺ ordered that those graves be dug up and what was in them removed. In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him): "There was in it [the site] what I tell you: graves of the polytheists, ruins, and palm trees. The Prophet ﷺ ordered the graves of the polytheists to be dug up, and they were dug up; then the ruins were leveled; and the palm trees were cut down, and they arranged the palm trees facing the qibla of the mosque, and made its two doorposts of stone." ... The hadith. This is the wording of al-Bukhari. The wording of Muslim is similar in meaning. The graves of the polytheists have no sanctity; therefore the Prophet ﷺ ordered them dug up and what was in them removed. So the place became as if there had never been a grave there at all, since it was entirely removed. This is clear, as you see. End quote.

The verified position beyond doubt is that it is not permissible to build upon graves or to plaster them (tajsis). As Muslim narrated in his Sahih, and others, from Abu al-Hayyaj al-Asadi: "Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said to him: Shall I not send you on the same errand the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me on? That you leave no statue without obliterating it, and no raised grave without leveling it."

And because it is established in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere, also from Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade that a grave be plastered, that one sit upon it, and that anything be built upon it."

This prohibition is established from him ﷺ, and he said: "When I forbid you from something, avoid it." And He, Exalted and Majestic, said: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾.

It has become clear from what we have mentioned the ruling on prayer in places of ground subsidence (al-khasf), in the graveyard, toward a grave, and in the bathhouse.

As for the camel pens (a'tan al-ibil): it is also established from the Prophet ﷺ that he forbade prayer in them. Muslim recorded in his Sahih, from the hadith of Jabir ibn Samurah (may Allah be pleased with him): "A man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Should I perform ablution after eating the flesh of sheep? He said: 'If you wish, perform ablution, and if you wish, do not perform ablution.' He said: Should I perform ablution after eating the flesh of camels? He said: 'Yes; perform ablution after eating the flesh of camels.' He said: Shall I pray in the resting places of sheep? He said: 'Yes.' He said: Shall I pray in the resting places of camels? He said: 'No.'" This is the wording of Muslim in his Sahih.

Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it sahih), and Ibn Majah recorded, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him): "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Pray in the resting places of sheep, and do not pray in the camel pens.'"

Al-Nasa'i, al-Bayhaqi, and Ibn Majah recorded, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mughaffal (may Allah be pleased with him): "The Prophet ﷺ forbade prayer in camel pens."

Al-Nawawi said in (Sharh al-Muhadhdhab): the chain by which al-Bayhaqi narrated it is hasan. Abu Dawud recorded in his Sunan, in the chapter on ablution from camel flesh and in the chapter on the prohibition of prayer in the resting places of camels, from al-Bara' ibn Azib (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about prayer in the resting places of camels, and he said: 'Do not pray in the resting places of camels, for they are from the devils.' He was asked about prayer in the resting places of sheep, and he said: 'Pray in them, for they are a blessing.'"

Ibn Majah recorded, from Abdullah ibn Amr, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "Pray in the sheepfolds, and do not pray in the camel pens."

Ibn Majah recorded, from Sabrah ibn Ma'bad al-Juhani (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Prayer is not to be performed in the camel pens, and prayer is to be performed in the sheepfolds."

Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, gave this question a chapter heading in his Sahih, saying: "Chapter: Prayer in the places of camels." Then he said: Sadaqah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Hayyan informed us, saying: Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Nafi', who said: "I saw Ibn Umar pray facing his camel, and he said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ do it."

Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath, in discussing this chapter heading, for which al-Bukhari did not bring a hadith that matches it, the following: It seems he is indicating that the hadiths reported concerning the distinction between camels and sheep are not up to his conditions, but they have strong chains: among them the hadith of Jabir ibn Samurah in Muslim, the hadith of al-Bara' ibn Azib in Abu Dawud, the hadith of Abu Hurairah in al-Tirmidhi, the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mughaffal in al-Nasa'i, and the hadith of Sabrah ibn Ma'bad in Ibn Majah. In most of them the expression is "camel pens" (ma'atin al-ibil). In the hadith of Jabir ibn Samurah and al-Bara' the wording is "resting places of camels" (mabarik al-ibil), and similar in the hadith of Sulayk in al-Tabarani; in the hadith of Sabrah, and likewise in the hadith of Abu Hurairah in al-Tirmidhi, the wording is "camel pens" (a'tan al-ibil). In the hadith of Usayd ibn Hudayr in al-Tabarani the wording is "kneeling places of camels" (manakh al-ibil), and in the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr in Ahmad the wording is "camel resting grounds" (marabid al-ibil). The author therefore used the general term "places" (mawadi'), since it is more comprehensive, while "ma'atin" is more specific than "mawadi'," because the ma'atin are the places where camels are kept near water specifically.

Some scholars held that the prohibition is specific to the ma'atin and not to other places where camels are found. It was also said that it covers their shelter in general, as transmitted by the author of al-Mughni from Ahmad. End of Ibn Hajar's words.

Ibn Hazm said: The hadiths prohibiting prayer in camel pens are mutawatir (widely transmitted) by a mass transmission that necessitates knowledge.

Once you know this, understand that the scholars differed over the validity of prayer in camel pens.

A group of the people of knowledge held that prayer there is not valid. This is the sound view in the school of Imam Ahmad, and most of his companions adhered to it.

The author of (al-Insaf) said: This is the school, and the companions hold it. In (al-Furu') it is the more famous and sounder opinion in the school. The author and others said: This is the apparent school position, and it is among the isolated views.

Among those who held this view is Ibn Hazm.

The majority of scholars held that the prohibition is for reprehensibility (karahah), and that if one prayed there his prayer would be valid. We have already mentioned the words of the usul scholars concerning such a question.

Know that the scholars differed over the reason for the prohibition of prayer in camel pens.

It was said: because they were created from the devils, as previously mentioned in the hadith from the Prophet ﷺ. This is the sound explanation of the reason, because the Prophet ﷺ said: "Do not pray in the resting places of camels, for they were created from the devils." His placing the statement that they were created from the devils after the prohibition with the particle "fa" (so/therefore) indicates that it is the cause of the ruling, as established in the discussion of the methods of indicating causation (masluk al-nass, masluk al-iima' wa al-tanbih).

A group of the people of knowledge said: the meaning of their being "created from the devils" is that they may bolt while one is in prayer, which leads to cutting off his prayer, or harming him, or distracting his attention. We have already mentioned that every rebellious, defiant creature the Arabs call a devil (shaytan). When camels bolt, they are rebellious and defiant, so naming them by the name of devils corresponds to the language of the Arabs.

The Arabs say "he was created from such-and-such" for emphasis, as they say "this was created from generosity," and from it is His saying: ﴿Man was created from haste﴾ [al-Anbiya: 37], according to the more correct of the two interpretations.

On this basis, a distinction is made between the camels being in their pens and their being absent from them, since their bolting is then safe from occurring.

Al-Shawkani said in (Nayl al-Awtar): The hadith of Ibn Mughaffal in Ahmad with a sahih chain guides to the correctness of this, with the wording: "Do not pray in camel pens, for they were created from the jinn. Do you not see their eyes and their forms when they bolt?"

It may also be possible that the reason for the prohibition is that they are brought to their pens after one has begun the prayer, so that they cut it off, or one continues in it while his attention is preoccupied. End of al-Shawkani's words.

From this explicitly stated reason, the scholars who hold that the prayer is not invalid understood that: since the reason for the prohibition is what has been mentioned, this indicates that if one performs the prayer complete, it is not invalid.

It was said: the reason is that the owners of camels defecate in their resting places, unlike the owners of sheep.

It was said: the reason is that the female camel menstruates and the male camel emits semen.

All of these are explanations on which no reliance is placed. The sound explanation is the one stated from him ﷺ, that they were created from the devils. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

* *

Note.

If it is asked: What is the ruling on prayer in the resting places of cattle?

The answer: most scholars say that they are like the sheepfolds. If it were said that they are like the camel pens, there would be a basis for that.

Ibn Hajar said (in Fath al-Bari): There occurs in the Musnad of Ahmad, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar: "The Prophet ﷺ used to pray in the sheepfolds and did not pray in the resting places of camels and cattle." End quote. He said: its chain is weak. If it were established, it would indicate that the ruling on cattle is the ruling on camels. This is contrary to what Ibn al-Mundhir mentioned: that cattle in this respect are like sheep. End of Ibn Hajar's words.

As for what Abu Dawud, may Allah have mercy on him, said, that acting on a weak hadith is better than acting on personal opinion (ra'y), it has a valid basis. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

As for prayer in a dunghill, a slaughterhouse, on the road's edge, and on top of the House of Allah, the Sacred House, the evidence for its prohibition is the hadith previously mentioned from Zayd ibn Jubayrah, from Dawud ibn Husayn, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ, and we have already mentioned what is said about its chain.

As for prayer toward the wall of a latrine that has filth on it, it is based on what has been reported of a prohibition of this from some of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them all).

The allamah al-Shawkani, may Allah have mercy on him, said in (Nayl al-Awtar): As for prayer toward the wall of a latrine, it is based on the hadith of Ibn Abbas, in seven Companions, with the wording: "He forbade prayer in the mosque facing a latrine (hush)," recorded by Ibn Adi. Al-Iraqi said its chain is not sound.

Ibn Abi Shaybah related in al-Musannaf, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: One should not pray facing a latrine.

And from Ali, who said: One should not pray facing a latrine.

(p-306) And from Ibrahim: They used to dislike three things... and he mentioned among them the latrine.

Concerning the disliking of facing it there is a difference among the scholars. End of al-Shawkani's words.

By "hush" (with the ḥā' vowelled either with a damma or a fatha) is meant the privy.

As for prayer in the church and the synagogue (the meaning of which is the places of worship of the Jews and Christians), a group of the people of knowledge disliked it.

Al-Nawawi said in (Sharh al-Madhhab): Ibn al-Mundhir related it from Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibn Abbas, and Malik (may Allah be pleased with them all).

Al-Shawkani said: Disliking it has also been reported from al-Hasan.

The compiler of this work, may Allah pardon him, says: The apparent meaning is that what has been reported of this from Umar and Ibn Abbas is not unrestricted, but refers specifically to churches and synagogues that contain images. What indicates this is what al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in his Sahih: he said, "Chapter: Prayer in the synagogue," and Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "We do not enter your churches because of the images that are in them." And Ibn Abbas used to pray in a synagogue except one that had images in it.

Ibn Hajar said in (al-Fath): The report that al-Bukhari gave in suspended form (ta'liq) from Umar, al-Razzaq connected through the route of Aslam, the freedman of Umar. The report given in suspended form from Ibn Abbas, al-Baghawi connected in al-Ja'diyyat. End quote.

It is known that al-Bukhari does not give a suspended report with a definitive form of attribution except what is established according to him.

A group of the people of knowledge permitted prayer in the church and the synagogue, among them Abu Musa, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, al-Sha'bi, Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, Ibn Sirin, al-Nakha'i, al-Awza'i, and others.

The allamah al-Shawkani, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Perhaps the basis for the disliking is what was mentioned earlier, the taking of the graves of their prophets and righteous people as mosques, since all synagogues and churches would then become a likely place for that.

The compiler of this work, may Allah pardon him, says: It is possible that the reason is that the church and the synagogue are places where Allah is disobeyed and disbelieved in, so they are a place of wrath and anger. As for the prohibition of prayer toward images, its evidence is established in the Sahih.

**Part 5 of 5**

Among the evidence for this is what al-Bukhari recorded in his Sahih, in the Book of Prayer. He said: "Chapter: If one prays in a garment with crosses (*musallab*) or pictures, does it invalidate his prayer, and what is prohibited in that? Abu Ma'mar 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Suhayb narrated to us, from Anas: 'Aisha had a *qiram* (a curtain with embroidered designs) with which she screened the side of her house. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Remove your *qiram* from us, for its pictures keep appearing to me in my prayer."'"

Al-Bukhari also said (in the Book of Clothing, Chapter: The Disliking of Clothing with Pictures): "Imran ibn Maysara narrated to us, 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Suhayb narrated to us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: 'Aisha had a *qiram* with which she screened the side of her house. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to her: "Remove it from me, for its pictures keep appearing to me in my prayer."'"

Muslim said in his Sahih: "Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'ba narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, who said: 'I heard al-Qasim narrating from 'Aisha that she had a garment with pictures stretched across a *sahwa* (a niche in the wall). The Prophet (ﷺ) would pray facing it, and he said: "Move it away from me." She said: "So I moved it and made it into cushions."'"

The garment in this narration is the *qiram* mentioned. *Qiram* (with a kasra on the qaf) means a curtain with embroidery and designs, or a thin curtain. From it is the saying of Labid in his Mu'allaqa, describing the litter (*hawdaj*):

"From every covered one that shades its poles, a pair upon which is a fine veil and its *qiram*."

And the saying of another, describing a dwelling:

"Upon the back of the sandy hill of al-'Ajuz, as if they were circles of embroidery upon the surface of a *qiram*."

The *killa* in Labid's verse is the *qiram* when it is sewn so that it becomes like a tent.

These authentic texts indicate that prayer facing images is not permissible. Among the evidence for this is what al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded in their two Sahihs from 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her: "Umm Habiba and Umm Salama mentioned a church they had seen in Abyssinia, containing pictures of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Those people, when a righteous man among them died, they built a mosque upon his grave and made those pictures in it. Those are the worst of creation in the sight of Allah on the Day of Resurrection.'" End. This is the wording of Muslim, and the wording of al-Bukhari is close to it. End.

As for the invalidity of the prayer of one who prays facing images, there is disagreement among the scholars, and al-Bukhari pointed to it (p-٣٠٨) with his statement quoted earlier: "Chapter: If one prays in a garment with crosses or pictures, does it invalidate his prayer?" etc.

We have already mentioned that the source of disagreement regarding invalidity is the disagreement over whether the aspect of prohibition can be separated from the aspect of command. And Allah knows best.

As for the prohibition of depicting living beings, the punishment of their makers on the Day of Resurrection with the severest punishment, their being commanded to bring to life what they depicted, and the fact that angels do not enter a place containing a picture or a dog, all of this is well known and established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

As for prayer in a usurped place: it is not permissible by the consensus of the Muslims, because staying there is unlawful outside of prayer, so it is all the more unlawful during prayer.

The majority of the scholars held that if one prays in usurped land, his prayer is valid, because the aspect (of prohibition) is separable: he is sinful for his usurpation, and obedient in his prayer, like one who prays while wearing silk.

Imam Ahmad, in the most authentic of the reports from him, and al-Jubba'i and others from the Mu'tazila, held that it is invalid, because the aspect of command cannot be separated from the aspect of prohibition, as we have mentioned. We have already mentioned the statements of the general body of scholars on this issue in the verses of *Maraqi al-Su'ud* that we cited.

As for the prohibition of praying facing a sleeping person or one who is speaking: its evidence is what Abu Dawud recorded in his Sunan. He said: "Chapter: Praying facing those who are talking or sleeping. 'Abdullah ibn Maslama al-Qa'nabi narrated to us, 'Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn Ayman narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq, from one who narrated to him, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: I said to him, meaning to 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas narrated to me that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not pray behind one who is sleeping or one who is speaking."'" End.

The weakness of this hadith is not hidden, because the narrator in this chain from Muhammad ibn Ka'b is unknown, as you see.

Ibn Majah said in his Sunan: "Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Abu al-Miqdam narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade praying behind one who is speaking or sleeping.'" The chain of Ibn Majah is also not to be used as evidence, because the narrator in it from Muhammad ibn Ka'b is Abu al-Miqdam, who is Hisham ibn Ziyad ibn Abi Yazid, who is Hisham ibn Abi Hisham, and he is also called Hisham ibn Abi al-Walid al-Madani, and he is not to be relied upon in narration. Ibn Hajar said about him in *al-Taqrib*: "Matruk" (abandoned). And in *Tahdhib al-Tahdhib* he said: 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad and Abu Zur'a said: "Weak in hadith." Al-Duri narrated from Ibn Ma'in: "Not trustworthy." In another place he said: "Weak, of no value." Al-Bukhari said: "They spoke about him." Abu Dawud said: "Not trustworthy." Al-Tirmidhi said: "He is weakened." Al-Nasa'i and 'Ali ibn al-Junayd al-Azdi said: "Matruk al-hadith." Al-Nasa'i also said: "Weak." Al-Nasa'i said: "Not trustworthy," and once: "Of no value." Abu Hatim said: "Weak in hadith, not strong; he was a neighbor of Abu al-Walid, and he did not narrate from him, and he did not approve of him. It is said that he took the book of Hafs al-Minqari from al-Hasan and narrated from al-Hasan, and in his narrations from al-Hasan there are denounced hadiths."

I say: Ibn Hibban said: "He narrates fabrications from trustworthy narrators; it is not permissible to argue with him." Al-Daraqutni said: "Weak," and Ibn al-Mubarak abandoned his hadith. Ibn Sa'd said: "He was weak in hadith." Abu Bakr ibn Khuzayma said: "His hadith is not to be used as evidence." Al-'Ijli said: "Weak." Ya'qub ibn Sufyan said: "Weak; his hadith is not to be rejoiced in." End of the words of Ibn Hajar. From this you know that the prohibition of praying facing a sleeping or speaking person has not been established through a sound chain.

Now, having known this, know that praying facing a sleeping person was established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he did it. Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih (Chapter: Praying behind one who is sleeping): "Musaddad narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from 'Aisha, who said: 'The Prophet (ﷺ) would pray while I was lying across his bed. When he wished to pray Witr, he would wake me, and I would pray Witr.'"

Ibn Hajar said in *al-Fath*: "He cited the hadith of 'Aisha also from another route with different wording, to indicate that someone may distinguish between her being asleep or awake. And it seems he also indicated the weakness of the hadith that prohibits praying facing a sleeper, which Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah recorded from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas." End. Abu Dawud said: "All its routes are feeble," meaning the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas. End.

On this topic there is also a report from Ibn 'Umar recorded by Ibn 'Adi, and from Abu Hurayra recorded by al-Tabarani in *al-Awsat*, and both of them are also feeble. Mujahid, Tawus and Malik disliked praying facing a sleeper, for fear that something might appear from him that would distract the worshipper from his prayer. The apparent indication of the author's (al-Bukhari's) practice is that there is no disliking where safety from that is assured. End of the words of Ibn Hajar in (*Fath al-Bari*).

The one who has restricted this (the author, Shinqiti, may Allah pardon him) says: What appears to me, and Allah the Most High knows best, is that no specific text has been established prohibiting prayer facing a sleeper or a speaker. But that does not preclude deriving disliking from the general meaning of other texts, such as the reason for disliking prayer facing a sleeper, namely the fear that something may appear from him that would distract the worshipper from his prayer, because the sleeper does not know what is happening with himself.

And like the reason for disliking prayer facing one who is speaking: that speech disturbs the worshipper in his prayer. And Allah the Most High knows best.

As for the disliking of praying in the valley bottom: it is supported by what has come in some narrations of the hadith of Zayd ibn Jubayra mentioned earlier, regarding the places in which prayer was forbidden, where "the bottom of the valley" appears instead of "the graveyard." Al-Shawkani said: al-Hafiz said: "This addition is false and not known."

Some scholars said: the disliking of prayer in the bottom of the valley is specific to the valley in which Satan appeared before the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions, so they slept through the dawn prayer until the sun rose. The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded them to move away from that place where Satan had appeared to them.

This is answered: Satan may have left that valley. And Allah the Most High knows best.

As for the prohibition of praying in the Mosque of Harm, its evidence is the saying of Allah the Most High: ﴿Do not stand in it ever﴾ [al-Tawba: 108], and His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief and division among the believers and as a station for whoever had warred against Allah and His Messenger before﴾ [al-Tawba: 107], the verse. And His saying: ﴿Is one who founded his building upon piety from Allah and approval better, or one who founded his building upon the edge of a crumbling cliff, so it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people. Their building which they constructed will not cease to be a doubt in their hearts unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾ [al-Tawba: 109–110], the verse. These verses indicate distance from the location of that mosque and not standing in it, as is evident.

As for the disliking of praying facing an oven (*tannur*): it is based on what Ibn Abi Shayba recorded in *al-Musannaf* from Muhammad ibn Sirin, that he disliked praying facing an oven and said: "It is a house of fire."

The apparent practice of al-Bukhari is that praying facing an oven is not disliked in his view, and that the presentation of the fire to the Prophet (ﷺ) during his prayer indicates the absence of disliking. Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih (Chapter: One who prays with an oven or fire in front of him, or something that is worshipped, intending thereby Allah): "Al-Zuhri said: Anas informed me, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'The Fire was presented to me while I was praying.' 'Abdullah ibn Maslama narrated to us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata ibn Yasar, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'The sun eclipsed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed, then he said: "I saw the Fire, and I have never seen a sight more terrible than today."'" End.

The presentation of the fire to him (ﷺ) while he was in his prayer is evidence of the absence of disliking, because he did not break off (his prayer).

Some authentic narrations in the Sahih indicate that the Fire was presented to him from the direction of his face, not from the right nor the left. In some authentic narrations, they said to him after he had turned away: "O Messenger of Allah, we saw you take something in your place, then we saw you *takaka'ta* (draw back) — that is, you withdrew — backward?" And in his answer: that was because he "was shown the Fire..." etc.

This is the summary of the scholars' statements regarding the places in which a prohibition on praying has been reported, which are related to the verse of al-Hijr that we are concerned with. And Allah the Most High knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 82:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they used to hew out of the mountains houses, secure.﴾

In this noble verse, He—exalted and most high—mentions that the people of al-Hijr, who are Thamud, the people of Salih, were secure in their homelands, and that they used to hew out the mountains into houses.

He clarified this meaning in other places,

• such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Will you be left in what is here, secure? ﴾ ﴿Among gardens and springs,﴾ ﴿and crops and palm trees whose spathes are soft [of fruit]﴾ ﴿And you hew out of the mountains, houses, exultant﴾ [al-Shu'ara’: 147–149],

• and His saying: ﴿And remember when He made you successors after the people of 'Ad and settled you in the land, you take for yourselves palaces from its plains and hew out the mountains into houses. So remember the favors of Allah﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-A'raf: 74],

• and His saying: ﴿And [of] Thamud, who cut out the rocks in the valley﴾ [al-Fajr: 9],

i.e., they cut the rock by hewing it into houses.

**The words of the Exalted: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾.**

In this noble verse, the Exalted mentions that He did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth; that is, so that it would thereby show that He is the one deserving to be worshipped alone, and that He imposes obligations upon creation and will recompense them for their deeds.

The verse thus indicates that He did not create in vain, nor in play, nor in falsehood. He has clarified this in many verses, such as:

• His saying: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire﴾ [Sad: 27].

• His saying: ﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain. Glory be to You, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾ [Al 'Imran: 191].

• His saying: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play. We did not create them except with truth﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 38–39], and the verse continues.

• His saying: ﴿Did you then suppose that We created you in vain and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ ﴿So exalted is Allah, the True King; there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 115–116],

• His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, that He may recompense those who did evil according to what they did and recompense those who did good with the best﴾ [An-Najm: 31],

• His saying: ﴿Does man think that he will be left neglected?﴾ ﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted?﴾ [Al-Qiyamah: 36–37].

And other verses besides these.

* *

**The words of the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, the Hour is coming﴾.**

In this noble verse, the Exalted mentions that the Hour is coming, and He emphasizes this with the particle of emphasis which is "inna", and with the lam of initiation, which the broken inna (the inna that is pronounced with a kasra) pushes from the subject to the predicate. This indicates two matters:

The first: that the coming of the Hour is certain.

The second: that its coming was denied by the disbelievers; because the multiplication of emphasis indicates the denial of the statement, as has been established in the science of rhetorical meanings (fann al-ma'ani).

He clarified these two matters in other verses. He made clear that the Hour is certainly coming in many places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming; I almost conceal it﴾ [Ta-Ha: 15],

• His saying: ﴿And that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt in it, and that Allah will resurrect those in the graves﴾ [Al-Hajj: 7],

• His saying: ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing.﴾ ﴿The Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget what she nursed, and every pregnant one will lay down her load﴾ ... and the verse continues [Al-Hajj: 1–2],

• His saying: ﴿And when it was said, "Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and the Hour, there is no doubt about it," you said, "We do not know what the Hour is"﴾ and the verse continues [Al-Jathiyah: 32],

• His saying: ﴿And the Day the Hour establishes itself, the criminals will despair﴾ [Ar-Rum: 12],

• His saying: ﴿And the Day the Hour establishes itself, the criminals will swear that they remained not but an hour﴾ [Ar-Rum: 55],

• His saying: ﴿Say, "Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None will reveal it at its time except Him. It has been heavy upon the heavens and the earth. It will not come to you except suddenly"﴾ [Al-A'raf: 187],

and verses similar to these are very many.

He – Majestic and Exalted – also made clear the disbelievers' denial of it in other places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us." Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you"﴾ [Saba': 3],

• His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected﴾ [At-Taghabun: 7],

• His saying: ﴿Indeed, these say﴾ ﴿"There is not but our first death, and we will not be resurrected"﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 34–35],

and verses similar to these are very many.

* *

**The words of the Exalted: ﴿So forgive with gracious forgiveness﴾.**

Allah, Majestic and Exalted, commanded His Prophet – peace and blessings be upon him – in this noble verse to forgive those who did evil with gracious forgiveness; that is, with forbearance and overlooking. 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas said: gracious forgiveness is contentment without reproach. His command (ﷺ) includes the wisdom of the community, because he is their exemplar and the one who legislates for them.

He, the Exalted, clarified this meaning in other places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿So overlook them and say, "Peace," for they will come to know﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 89],

• His saying: ﴿And when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace"﴾ [Al-Furqan: 63],

• His saying: ﴿And when they hear vain speech, they turn away from it and say, "To us are our deeds and to you are your deeds. Peace be upon you; we do not seek the ignorant"﴾ [Al-Qasas: 55],

• His saying: ﴿So pardon and overlook until Allah brings His command﴾ and the verse continues [Al-Baqarah: 109].

and other verses besides these.

Some scholars said: this command to overlook is abrogated (mansukh) by the verses of the sword (naskh, abrogation of a ruling by a later ruling). It was also said: it is not abrogated, and what is meant by it is good conduct in opposition, which is dealing with good character.

Al-Jawhari said in his Sihah: "Khuluq" is disposition (sajiyyah); it is said: "Khalisi al-mu'min" and "Khaliqi al-fajir" (meet the believer with good character and the wicked with his own manner).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 86:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is the Creator, the All-Knowing.﴾

He - exalted and majestic is He - mentioned in this noble verse that He is the Creator (al-Khallaq), the All-Knowing (al-'Alim). Both al-Khallaq and al-'Alim are intensive forms (sighat mubalaghah, forms denoting emphasis and intensity).

The verse indicates that the Creator cannot be described as being a creator except that He is All-Knowing of everything, nothing being hidden from Him, since one who is ignorant of a thing cannot create it.

He clarified this meaning in many verses, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is, of all creation, Knowing."﴾ [Ya-Sin: 79],

• and His saying: ﴿Does He not know who created? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.﴾ [al-Mulk: 14],

• and His saying: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come [into being], willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We come willingly." Then He completed them as seven heavens in two days and inspired in each heaven its command. And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and as protection. That is the decree of the Exalted in Might, the All-Knowing.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 29],

• and His saying: ﴿Allah is the One who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them. The command descends among them that you may know that Allah is over all things competent and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge.﴾ [at-Talaq: 12],

• and His saying, exalted is He, answering the disbelievers when they denied the Resurrection and said: ﴿When we have died and become dust - that is a return far-fetched.﴾ [Qaf: 3], making clear that the One who knows what the earth has consumed of their bodies is capable of bringing them back to life: ﴿We know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserved record.﴾ [Qaf: 4],

and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 87:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated [verses] and the great Qur'an﴾. In this noble verse, He, may He be glorified and exalted, mentions that He gave His Prophet ﷺ seven of the oft-repeated [verses] and the great Qur'an, but He does not clarify here what is meant by that.

We have already mentioned, in the introduction to this blessed book, that if a noble verse has an explanation in the Book of Allah which is not sufficient for the intended meaning, we complete that explanation from the Sunnah, clarifying the Book by the Sunnah insofar as it is an explanation of the Clear Qur'an (using the active participle). Knowing this, you should know that the Prophet ﷺ clarified in the authentic hadith that what is meant by the seven oft-repeated [verses] and the great Qur'an in this noble verse is the Opening of the Book (Fatihat al-Kitab). So the Opening of the Book clarifies what is meant by the seven oft-repeated [verses] and the great Qur'an, and I have only explained that (p-315) by the Prophet ﷺ's clarification of it in the authentic hadith.

Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih, in the interpretation of this noble verse: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me, Ghundar narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Khubayb ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Hafs ibn 'Asim, "from Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla, who said: The Prophet ﷺ passed by me while I was praying, and he called me, but I did not come to him until I had finished praying. Then I came, and he said: 'What prevented you from coming to me?' I said: 'I was praying.' He said: 'Did not Allah say: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger﴾ [al-Anfal: 24]? Then he said: Shall I not teach you the greatest surah in the Qur'an before I leave the mosque?' The Prophet ﷺ then went to leave, and I reminded him, and he said: ﴿All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Fatihah: 2]. It is the seven oft-repeated [verses], and the great Qur'an which I was given.'" Adam narrated to us, Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, Sa'id al-Maqbari narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'The Mother of the Qur'an is the seven oft-repeated [verses], and the great Qur'an.'"

This is a sound text from the Prophet ﷺ that what is meant by the seven oft-repeated [verses] and the great Qur'an is the Opening of the Book. By this you know that the saying of whoever said that they are the seven long [surahs] is not correct, since there is no speech for anyone in the presence of his (ﷺ) [statement]. Among what indicates the invalidity of that view is that this verse of al-Hijr is Meccan, and the seven long [surahs] were only revealed in Medina. And Allah knows best.

It was said that it is called "oft-repeated" (mathani) because its recitation is repeated in the prayer.

It was said that it is called "seven" (sab') because it has seven verses.

It was said that it is called "the great Qur'an" because it is the greatest surah, as was established from the Prophet ﷺ in the authentic hadith mentioned just above.

As for why "the great Qur'an" is joined by conjunction to "the seven oft-repeated [verses]", even though both refer to one thing, namely the Opening: it is known in the Arabic language that when one thing is mentioned with two different attributes, it is permissible to conjoin one of them to the other, treating the difference of attributes as the difference of essences. An example of this is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ ﴿Who created and proportioned﴾ ﴿And who determined and guided﴾ ﴿And who brought out the pasture﴾ [al-A'la: 1–4], and the saying of the poet:

"To the sovereign lord and son of the hero, and the lion of the battalion in the crowd."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 88:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do not extend your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to of them, [the various] pairs [of disbelievers]﴾.

When Exalted is He explained that He had given the Prophet ﷺ the seven oft-repeated [verses] and the great Qur'an, which is the greatest portion and the greatest share with Allah, Exalted is He, He forbade him to extend his eyes toward the goods of the worldly life with which He had given enjoyment to the disbelievers. This is because whoever has been given by his Lord, Majestic and Exalted, the greatest portion and the most abundant share, should not look at the lowest, most contemptible portion, especially when its owner was given it only for the sake of trial and testing. He clarified this meaning in other places, such as His saying in (Ta-Ha): ﴿So be patient over what they say, and glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾ ﴿And during the periods of the night glorify [Him], and at the ends of the day, that you may be pleased﴾ ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [various] pairs of them, the splendor of the worldly life, that We may test them therein. But the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting﴾ ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast therein. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you, and the best outcome is for righteousness﴾ [Ta-Ha: 130–132]. The meaning of "pairs" (azwaj) here is: categories of those whom Allah has given enjoyment of the world.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not grieve over them﴾.

The correct meaning of this noble verse is that Allah forbade His Prophet ﷺ from grieving over the disbelievers when they refuse to accept Islam. What supports this is the frequent occurrence of this meaning in the Great Qur'an.

• Such as His saying: ﴿And do not grieve over them or be in distress because of what they plot﴾ [An-Nahl: 127],

• And His saying: ﴿So do not let yourself go in pursuit of them, expiring with regret﴾ [Fatir: 8],

• And His saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers﴾,

• And His saying: ﴿Then perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their traces if they do not believe in this discourse, [out of] sorrow﴾ [Al-Kahf: 6],

• And His saying: ﴿And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 68],

along with other verses.

The meaning is: you have conveyed, and you are not responsible for their wretchedness if they refuse faith. Your duty is only to convey, and upon Us is the reckoning. So do not grieve over them if they are wretched.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And lower your wing to the believers﴾.

Allah, Majestic and Exalted, commanded His Prophet in this noble verse to lower his wing to the believers. Lowering the wing is a metaphor for gentleness of disposition and humility, and from it is the saying of the poet:

"You are renowned for lowering the wing, so do not be, in raising it, a falcon."

He clarified this meaning in other places, such as His saying in (ash-Shu'ara'): ﴿And lower your wing to those who follow you among the believers﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 215], and His saying: ﴿So by mercy from Allah, you were lenient with them. And if you had been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have disbanded from around you. So pardon them, and ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter﴾ [Al-Imran: 159], along with other verses.

(p-317) What is understood from the implicit meaning (mafhum al-mukhalafa) of this noble verse, namely its converse meaning, is that the wing is not lowered toward those who are not believers; rather, they are dealt with harshness and severity.

Exalted is He has clarified this converse meaning in other places:

• Such as His saying: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh upon them﴾ [At-Tawbah: 73 and 66],

• And His saying: ﴿Hard against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves﴾ [Al-Fath: 29],

• And His saying: ﴿Humble toward the believers, mighty over the disbelievers﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 54],

as we have mentioned earlier in "Al-Ma'idah".

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 90:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿As We sent down upon the dividers﴾.

Concerning the meaning of "the dividers" (al-muqtasimin), there are well-known opinions among the scholars, and each one of them is supported by a Qur'an verse. However, in the noble verse there is an indication (qarinah) that weakens some of these opinions:

The first: that the intended meaning of "the dividers" is those who swear oaths to deny the messengers and oppose them. According to this view, al-iqtisam (the dividing) is an iftiʿal (reflexive form) from al-qasam (oath) in the sense of yamin (oath), and it means mutual swearing.

Among the verses that point to this interpretation is His saying, may He be exalted, about the people of Salih: ﴿They said: "Swear to one another by Allah that we will surely attack him and his family by night"﴾ [an-Naml: 49], that is, we will kill them at night. And His saying: ﴿And they swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that Allah will not resurrect those who die﴾ [an-Nahl: 38]. And His saying: ﴿Had you not sworn before that there would be for you no decline?﴾ [Ibrahim: 44]. And His saying: ﴿Are these the ones of whom you swore that Allah would not grant them mercy?﴾ [al-Araf: 49], and other verses besides these. It is as if they would not deny anything without swearing to it, so they were called "dividers" (muqtasimin).

The second opinion: that the intended meaning of "the dividers" is the Jews and the Christians. They were described as "dividers" because they divided their scriptures, believing in some of them and disbelieving in others.

What supports this view is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 85], and His saying: ﴿And they say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others"﴾ [an-Nisa: 150].

The third opinion: that the intended meaning of "the dividers" is a group of the disbelievers of Makkah who divided the Qur'an by their false sayings. Some of them said: it is poetry; some said: it is sorcery; some said: it is soothsaying; some said: it is the fables of the ancients; and some said: Muhammad (ﷺ) invented it.

This opinion is supported by the verses that indicate that they said these fabricated, false sayings about the Qur'an,

- such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe. And not the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember﴾ [al-Haqqah: 41-42],
- and His saying: ﴿So he said, "This is not but magic transmitted"﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 24],
- and His saying: ﴿This is not but an invention﴾ [Sad: 7],
- and His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "What has your Lord sent down?" they say, "Legends of the former peoples"﴾ [an-Nahl: 24],
- and His saying: ﴿And they say, "Legends of the former peoples, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening"﴾ [al-Furqan: 5], and other verses besides these. The indication in the noble verse supports this third opinion, and does not contradict the second, unlike the first; because His saying: ﴿who have made the Qur'an into parts﴾ [al-Hijr: 91] is more evident in the third opinion, since they made it into separate parts according to the variation of their false sayings, such as their saying: poetry, sorcery, soothsaying, etc.

And according to the view that they are the People of the Book, the intended meaning of "the Qur'an" is their scriptures which they divided into parts, believing in some of them and disbelieving in others; or it is the Qur'an itself, because they believed in what agreed with their desires from it and disbelieved in other than that.

As for His saying ﴿ʿidin﴾ [al-Hijr: 91], it is the plural of ʿidah, which is a part (ʿudw) of a thing, that is, they made it into separate parts. The omitted lam (radical) of the word is originally a waw. Some scholars said: the omitted lam is originally a ha', and accordingly the origin of ʿidah is ʿidhah. And al-ʿadhah means sorcery. So according to this view, the meaning is: they made the Qur'an into sorcery, like His saying: ﴿This is not but magic transmitted﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 24], and His saying: ﴿They said, "Two kinds of magic supporting each other"﴾ [al-Qasas: 48], and other verses besides these.

The Arabs call a sorcerer ʿadhih (ʿāḍih), a female sorcerer ʿadhihah, and sorcery ʿadhah. It is said that this is the dialect of Quraysh. From it is the saying of the poet:

I seek refuge in my Lord from the blowers (an-nafithat) in the knots of the sorceress, the bewitcher.

Note.

If it is said: with what is the kaf (as) in His saying, ﴿As We sent down upon the dividers﴾ [al-Hijr: 90] connected?

The answer is what az-Zamakhshari mentioned in his Kashshaf. He said: If you say, with what is His saying ﴿As We sent down﴾ connected? I say: there are two views. One of them is that it is connected to His saying ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated [verses]﴾ [al-Hijr: 87], that is: We sent down to you the like of what We sent down upon the People of the Book, who are the dividers who made the Qur'an into parts, when they said in their obstinacy and hostility: some of it is true, agreeing with the Torah and the Gospel, and some of it is false, opposing them; so they divided it into true and false, and broke it into parts. It was also said: they used to mock him, so one of them would say, "Surat al-Baqarah is mine," and another would say, "Surat Al 'Imran is mine," until he said: The second view is that it is connected to His saying ﴿And say, "Indeed, I am the clear warner"﴾ [al-Hijr: 89], that is: warn the Quraysh of the like of what We sent down as punishment upon the dividers (meaning the Jews), which befell Qurayzah and an-Nadir. He made the expected event like the occurred event, and this is part of the miraculous nature (ijaz), because it is a report of what will be and had already been. End of the point of relevance from the words of the author of the Kashshaf.

Abu Hayyan transmitted his words in full in "al-Bahr al-Muhit," and then Abu Hayyan said:

As for the first view, namely the connection of "kama" [al-Hijr: 90] with "ataynaka" [al-Hijr: 87], Abu al-Baqa mentioned it on the basis of an estimated (muqaddar) term, which is that it occupies a position in the accusative as an adjective (naʿt) of a deleted verbal noun (masdar) whose estimate is: "We gave you the seven of the oft-repeated [verses] as a giving like what We sent down," or "as a sending down like what We sent down"; because "ataynaka" has the meaning of "We sent down to you."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 94:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So proclaim openly what you are commanded﴾.

That is: openly declare it and make it manifest, from the expression "ṣadaʿa bil-ḥujjah" (he stated the proof openly), when he speaks it aloud, just as you would say "ṣarraḥa bihā" (he stated it clearly).

In this noble verse, Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to convey what he was commanded openly, without concealment or equivocation. He clarified this meaning in many places, such as His saying: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67].

Allah, the Exalted, has also testified that he complied with that command and conveyed it in the most complete manner in other places, such as His saying: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3], and His saying: ﴿So turn away from them; you are not to be blamed﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 54], and other verses besides these.

Note (tanbīh).

As for His saying: fa-ṣdaʿ [al-Hijr: 94], some scholars said: its root is from ṣadʿ (splitting) in the sense of manifestation, and from it comes their saying: "inṣadaʿa al-ṣubḥ" (the dawn broke open), meaning the night split apart from it. And al-ṣadīʿ means the dawn, because it breaks open (infiṣāduh). From it is the saying of ʿAmr ibn Maʿdikarib:

*You see the wolf spreading out its forelegs, as if the whiteness of its chest were a dawn (ṣadīʿ).*

That is, dawn. The meaning according to this view is: make manifest what you are commanded, and convey it openly before the witnesses. The Arabs say: "ṣadaʿtu al-shayʾ" (I made the thing manifest). From it is the saying of Abu Dhu'ayb: (p-320)

*And as if those (arrows) were a ribāba, and as if he were a yasar, pouring forth over the arrows and striking/dividing them*

This is what the author of Lisan al-Arab reported.

Other scholars said: its root is from ṣadʿ in the sense of separating and cleaving a hard thing, such as glass or a wall. From it, in the sense of separating, is His saying: ﴿Before there comes a Day from Allah which cannot be turned back. On that Day they will be separated (yaṣṣaddaʿūn)﴾ [ar-Rum: 43], that is, they will divide: a group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿And the Day the Hour is established, on that Day they will be divided﴾ [ar-Rum: 14]. From it is the saying of Ghaylan Dhu al-Rummah:

*On the evening when my heart was split between the one who stayed and the one who departed, the split (ṣadīʿ) went off with the departing ones.*

He means: his heart divided into two parts: a part with the one who stayed and a part with those who departed.

According to this view, fa-ṣdaʿ bi-mā tu'mar means: separate truth from falsehood by what Allah has commanded you to convey. His saying "bi-mā tu'mar" may allow that "mā" is a relative pronoun, and it may allow that it is a verbal-noun particle (maṣdariyyah), based on the permissibility of forming a verbal noun from "an" and a passive verb; a group of Arabic grammarians forbade this. Abu Hayyan said in (al-Bahr): the correct view is that this is not permissible.

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And turn away from the polytheists﴾.

There are two well-known opinions of the scholars concerning this noble verse:

The first: the meaning of ﴿And turn away from the polytheists﴾ is: do not be concerned with their denial and mockery, and let that not be difficult for you, for Allah is your protector from them.

According to this interpretation, the meaning of the verse is: ﴿So proclaim what you are commanded﴾, that is, convey the message of your Lord, ﴿and turn away from the polytheists﴾, that is, do not be concerned with them and do not fear them. This meaning is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67].

The second view, which is the apparent meaning of the verse: that at the beginning of the matter he was commanded to turn away from the polytheists, and then this was abrogated (nusikha) by the verses of the sword. Among the verses indicating this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord; there is no deity except Him, and turn away from the polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 106], and His saying: ﴿So turn away from them and wait; indeed they are waiting﴾ [as-Sajdah: 30], and His saying: ﴿So turn away from one who turns away from Our remembrance and desires only the worldly life﴾ [an-Najm: 29], and His saying: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their harm﴾ [al-Ahzab: 48], (p-321) and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 95:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We suffice you against the mockers﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, makes clear that He sufficed His Prophet (ﷺ) against the mockers who used to ridicule him, and they were a group from Quraysh. In other places He mentions that He sufficed him against others, such as His saying concerning the People of the Book: ﴿So Allah will suffice you against them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 137], and His saying: ﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?﴾ [al-Zumar: 36], and other verses besides these.

The mockers mentioned are: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-'As ibn Wa'il, al-Harith ibn Qays al-Sahmi, al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth, and al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib.

The calamities that were the cause of their destruction are well known in history.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 97:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We know that your breast is constricted by what they say﴾.

In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that He knows that His Prophet ﷺ is distressed in his breast by what the disbelievers say about him, of disparagement, denial, and slander against the Qur'an. He clarified this meaning in other passages, such as:

• His saying: ﴿We indeed know that what they say grieves you﴾ [al-An'am: 33],

• and His saying: ﴿Perhaps you would leave out some of what is revealed to you, and your breast would be constricted by it, because they say, "Why has a treasure not been sent down to him, or an angel not come with him?"﴾ [Hud: 12],

• and His saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over them, if they do not believe in this message, out of sorrow﴾ [al-Kahf: 6],

• and His saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself, [O Muhammad], that they will not be believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 3],

in addition to other verses. We have already presented some of that in our commentary on "al-An'am" (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 98:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise, and be among those who prostrate.﴾

In this verse, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, commands His Prophet ﷺ with two matters: the first is His saying: ﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise﴾ [al-Hijr: 98], and the second is His saying: ﴿and be among those who prostrate﴾ [al-Hijr: 98].

Allah, Exalted, has repeated in His Book the command to do the two things mentioned in this noble verse, such as:

• His saying in the first case: ﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾ [an-Nasr: 3],

• and His saying: ﴿So be patient over what they say, and glorify your Lord with His praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾ [Ta-Ha: 130],

• and His saying: ﴿So be patient. Indeed, the promise of Allah is true. And ask forgiveness for your sin and glorify your Lord with praise in the evening and the morning﴾ [Ghafir: 55],

and verses of this kind are many.

The root meaning of tasbih (glorification, i.e. declaring Allah free of imperfection) in the language is: distancing from evil. Its meaning in the usage of the Sharia is: declaring Allah, Majestic and Exalted, free of everything that does not befit His majesty and perfection. The meaning of "sabbih" is: declare your Lord, Majestic and Exalted, free of everything that does not befit His perfection and majesty. His saying ﴿with His praise﴾ means: while you are engaged with the praise of your Lord, that is, with praising Him by all that He deserves of attributes of perfection and majesty. Because the phrase ﴿with the praise of your Lord﴾ is a construct linked to a definite noun, it encompasses all praises from every attribute of perfection and majesty established for Allah, Majestic and Exalted. Thus the noble verse comprises praise for every perfection, because perfection occurs through two matters:

The first: freedom from vices, and remoteness from what does not befit, and this is the meaning of tasbih.

The second: adorning oneself with virtues and being characterized by attributes of perfection, and this is the meaning of hamd (praise). Thus praise is complete with every perfection.

Because of this meaning, it is established in the Sahih from him ﷺ that he said: (( "Two words, light on the tongue, heavy in the Scale, beloved to the Most Merciful: Subhan Allahi wa bihamdihi (Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him), Subhan Allahi al-'Azim (Glory be to Allah, the Mighty)." ))

• And His saying in the second matter, which is prostration: ﴿No! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near [to Allah]﴾ [al-'Alaq: 19],

• and His saying: ﴿And of the night, prostrate to Him and glorify Him a long part of the night﴾ [al-Insan: 26],

• and His saying: ﴿And prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him you worship﴾ [Fussilat: 37].

In the Noble Qur'an, the application of tasbih to prayer is frequent.

A group of scholars said: what is meant by His saying ﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise﴾ [al-Hijr: 98] is: pray to Him. Accordingly, His saying ﴿and be among those who prostrate﴾ is an instance of mentioning the specific after the general (ʿatf al-khass ʿala al-ʿamm), and prayer includes the utmost of declaring Allah free of imperfection and the furthest limit of sanctification. In any case, what is meant by His saying ﴿and be among those who prostrate﴾ is: be among those who pray, whether we say that what is meant by tasbih is prayer, or that it is more general than that, including declaring Allah free of what does not befit Him. Because the intended prostration is prayer, this place was not a place of prostration according to the majority of scholars, contrary to one who claimed that it is a place of prostration.

Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir: Ibn al-'Arabi said: Some people thought that what is meant by the command here is prostration itself, so they considered this place a place of prostration in the Qur'an. I have seen the imam at the Mihrab of Zakariyya in Bayt al-Maqdis, may Allah purify it, prostrate at this place, and I prostrated with him there, but the majority of scholars did not regard it as such.

I say: Abu Bakr al-Naqqash has mentioned that there is a prostration here according to Abu Hudhayfa and Yaman ibn Ri'ab, and he regarded it as obligatory. End of al-Qurtubi's words.

The meaning of prostration has already been mentioned in Surat (( ar-Ra'd )). Based on the meaning that tasbih is prayer, the justification for this elaboration, which is the mention of the specific after the general, is the importance of prostration, because the servant is nearest to his Lord while he is in prostration.

Muslim said in his Sahih: And Harun ibn Ma'ruf and 'Amr ibn Sawad narrated to us, both saying: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, from 'Umarah ibn Ghaziyya, from Sumayy, the freedman of Abu Bakr, that he heard Abu Salih Dhakwan narrating from Abu Hurayra: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating; so increase in supplication."

Note

Know that the Exalted's ordering of the command to glorify and prostrate upon the constriction of his ﷺ chest because of what they say to him of evil is evidence that prayer and tasbih are a means of removing that distress; for this reason, whenever a matter distressed him ﷺ, he would hasten to prayer. And Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45], and so on.

This is supported by what Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated from the hadith of Nu'aym ibn Hammar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah the Exalted said: 'O son of Adam, do not fail to [perform] four rak'ahs at the beginning of the day, and I will suffice you at its end.'" So it is fitting for the Muslim, when a distress befalls him, to turn to Allah the Exalted with various kinds of acts of worship, including prayer and others.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 15, verse 99:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And worship your Lord﴾.

Allah, Majestic and Exalted, commanded His Prophet ﷺ to worship his Lord, meaning to draw near to Him in a manner of humility, submission and love, by means of all the acts of obedience with which he was commanded to draw near to Him, in the prescribed manner. Most of the Qur'an is devoted to realizing this command, which is the affirmative share of "There is no god but Allah," together with its negative share. The Qur'an has made clear that this benefits only when the second part of the declaration of Tawhid (monotheism) is realized, which is its negative share, namely renouncing all objects of worship other than Allah the Exalted in all kinds of worship. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So worship Him and rely upon Him﴾ [Hud: 123], and He said ﴿So worship Him and be steadfast in His worship﴾ [Maryam: 65], and He said: ﴿And worship Allah and associate nothing with Him﴾ [An-Nisa': 36], and He said ﴿So whoever disbelieves in Taghut and believes in Allah has grasped the most trustworthy handhold﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 256], and He said: ﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah except while associating others with Him﴾ [Yusuf: 106]. The verses of this kind are very numerous.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿until there comes to you the certainty﴾.

A group of the people of knowledge, among them Salim ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others, said: (p-324) "The certainty" (al-yaqin) is death. What supports this is the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿They will say, "We were not of those who prayed. And we did not used to feed the poor. And we used to engage in vain discourse with those who engaged in it. And we used to deny the Day of Judgment, until there came to us the certainty"﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 43-47], and it is death.

This is also supported by what al-Bukhari recorded in his Sahih from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Kharijah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit, from Umm al-'Ala' (a woman of the Ansar): "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon 'Uthman ibn Maz'un when he had died. Umm al-'Ala' said: 'May the mercy of Allah be upon you, Abu al-Sa'ib! My testimony concerning you is that Allah has honoured you.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'And how do you know that Allah has honoured him?' She said: 'May my father and mother be ransom for you, O Messenger of Allah, then who will Allah honour?' He said: 'As for him, certainty has come to him, and I hope for good for him...'" The hadith. This sound hadith indicates that "the certainty" is death. The view of the one who said that what is meant by the certainty is the disclosure of the reality and the certain knowledge of the fact does not contradict what we have mentioned, because when death comes to a person, the reality becomes manifest to him with certainty. Al-Tihami excelled in his saying:

"Life is sleep, and death is wakefulness, and a person between them is a wandering phantom."

Sahib al-Durr al-Manthur said: Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim in his Tarikh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Daylami recorded, from Abu Muslim al-Khawlani, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I was not commanded to gather wealth and be among the merchants, but I was commanded: ﴿So exalt your Lord with praise and be among those who prostrate, and worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾" [Al-Hijr: 98-99].

Ibn Mardawayh recorded from Ibn Mas'ud - may Allah be pleased with him - from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "I was not commanded to gather wealth and be among the merchants, but I was commanded: ﴿So exalt your Lord with praise and be among those who prostrate, and worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾."

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Daylami recorded from Abu al-Darda' - may Allah be pleased with him: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "I was not commanded to be a merchant, nor to gather abundant wealth, but I was commanded: ﴿So exalt your Lord with praise and be among those who prostrate, and worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾."

Two points of caution.

The first: this noble verse indicates that a person, as long as he is alive and has sound reason by which he distinguishes, worship is obligatory upon him according to his capacity. If he cannot pray standing, let him pray sitting; if he cannot, then lying on his side. Likewise Allah said of His Prophet 'Isa - peace and blessings be upon him and upon our Prophet: ﴿And He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive﴾ [Maryam: 31]. Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih, "Chapter: If he is unable to sit, let him pray on his side." 'Ata' said: If he cannot turn to the qiblah, he prays wherever he faces. 'Abdan related to us from 'Abd Allah, from Ibrahim ibn Tahman, who said: al-Husayn al-Muktib related to me, from Buraydah, from 'Imran ibn Husayn - may Allah be pleased with both of them - who said: "I had hemorrhoids, so I asked the Prophet ﷺ about prayer, and he said: 'Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; if you cannot, then on your side.'" End of quote.

Similar to this is well known. Allah said: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [At-Taghabun: 16], and Allah said: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 286], and the Prophet ﷺ said: "When I command you to do something, do of it what you are able..." The hadith.

The second point: know that what some of the heretical disbelievers who claim Sufism interpret this noble verse by is that the meaning of "certainty" is knowledge of Allah the Exalted, and that the verse indicates that when the servant attains from knowledge of Allah that degree expressed as "certainty," the acts of worship and obligations fall from him, because that certainty is the ultimate aim of the command to worship. Interpreting the verse in this way is disbelief in Allah and heresy, and an exit from the religion of Islam by the consensus of the Muslims. This kind of thing is not called ta'wil (interpretation) in the technical sense; rather it is called play (la'ib), as we have previously stated in "Al 'Imran." It is known that the prophets - may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them and upon their companions - are the most knowledgeable of people about Allah, and the most aware of His rights, His attributes, and the glorification He deserves, and they were, along with that, the most abundant of people in worship of Allah the Exalted, and the most fearful of Him and the most hopeful of His mercy. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear Allah﴾ [Fatir: 28]. And knowledge is with Allah the Exalted.
